qa_answers.answer_text: Verified Marisol's McKinsey tenure (Bogotá office, 2018–2022, agribusiness practice) via the alumni directory and a former engagement manager. She left to build Lattice after repeatedly seeing the same problem across agribusiness clients: co-ops run on spreadsheets and a legacy on-prem tool (Cropsifter) that predates smartphones. Wharton MBA 2020 confirmed.

Founder-market fit is the strongest signal here. Marisol grew up on a coffee farm in Antioquia that her brother still runs — it was the first pilot co-op. She speaks the customer's language literally and figuratively, which shows up in the deck's retention numbers and in reference calls with two co-op managers who described her as "one of us."

On the FX question: co-ops are billed in local currency (MXN/COP) but the deck reports ARR in USD at spot. Marisol confirmed they have not hedged and re-price annually. At seed scale this is tolerable, but a 10–15% currency move would swing reported ARR materially — partner should treat the USD ARR figure as approximate and ask for the local-currency book.

scores.rationale: Large, fragmented LatAm co-op base with a beatable on-premise incumbent (Cropsifter) and digitization tailwinds.
Mobile-first workflow product with confirmed daily use at reference co-ops. Solid but not yet technically differentiated.
$480K ARR at 18% MoM is strong for the motion, but the base is small and 62% concentrated in three co-ops.
Per-member subscription is sensible, but no financial model was provided and unhedged FX makes reported ARR approximate.
Incumbent is weak; defensibility rests on workflow embedding and founder relationships rather than a structural moat.
$12M post on ~$480K ARR is a typical seed multiple for a domain-native team with real traction.
Exceptional founder-market fit: Marisol is ex-McKinsey agribusiness, raised on a co-op coffee farm that became the first pilot. Partner to assign the team score.

paragraphs.prose: Lattice is a mobile-first management platform for agricultural co-operatives in Latin America, replacing the spreadsheets and legacy on-premise software (Cropsifter) that co-ops use to track members, harvests, payments, and inputs. The company is at $480K ARR across 14 paying co-ops in Mexico and Colombia, growing 18% month-over-month. It was founded by Marisol Vega (CEO, ex-McKinsey agribusiness practice, raised on a Colombian coffee farm) and Tomás Aguirre (CTO, ex-Globant). Lattice is raising a $3M seed at a $12M post-money valuation; Hemrock would take $1M for a target ~8% stake. The thesis is that LatAm agriculture is digitizing a decade behind its US/EU peers, the incumbent is an unmaintained on-prem product, and a founder with genuine domain roots can win the category co-op by co-op.

Two issues must be resolved before a commitment. First, customer concentration is high: the top 3 co-ops represent 62% of ARR, so the loss of a single anchor would materially impair the growth story — the partner should understand contract length and switching costs for those three. Second, the data room is incomplete: there is no financial model (so unit economics and runway are unverified) and no cap table (so existing dilution is unknown). A secondary concern is FX — ARR is billed in MXN/COP but reported in USD unhedged, making the headline figure sensitive to currency moves.
[Partner to complete]

Lattice sells a smartphone-based SaaS to agricultural co-operatives, which are member-owned organizations that aggregate smallholder farmers to buy inputs and sell crops collectively. The product digitizes member registries, harvest intake and weigh-ins, per-member payment ledgers, and input distribution — workflows that co-ops run today on paper and Excel or on Cropsifter, an on-premise desktop tool from the pre-smartphone era. Current footprint is 14 paying co-ops across Mexico and Colombia, ranging from ~200 to ~4,000 members each.

There are tens of thousands of agricultural co-ops across Latin America managing a large share of the region's coffee, cacao, and produce output. The incumbent software (Cropsifter) is on-premise, predates mobile, and has roughly 150 co-op customers — a proof that co-ops will pay for software, and that the incumbent is beatable on form factor. Digitization tailwinds (smartphone penetration, buyer traceability requirements, and government formalization programs) are pulling co-ops toward modern tooling. The near-term obtainable market is smaller than the headline given fragmentation and long, relationship-driven sales cycles, but the category has a defensible wedge for a domain-native founder.

Two-person founding team. Marisol Vega (CEO) spent four years in McKinsey's Bogotá office in the agribusiness practice (2018–2022, verified via alumni directory and a former manager) and holds a Wharton MBA (2020); she grew up on a coffee farm in Antioquia that her family still operates. Tomás Aguirre (CTO) was an engineer at Globant before co-founding Lattice. The pairing is a domain-and-go-to-market lead with a hands-on technical co-founder.

Founder-market fit is unusually direct: Marisol's family co-op was Lattice's first pilot, and reference calls with two co-op managers described her as a genuine insider rather than a software vendor. Her McKinsey agribusiness work gives her a portfolio view of how dozens of co-ops operate, and the domain relationships shorten what is otherwise a trust-heavy, relationship-driven sales cycle. This is the single strongest element of the deal.
[Partner to complete — character assessment, founder-market fit judgment, and overall team score]

Company-stated traction is $480K ARR across 14 co-ops with 18% month-over-month growth. The growth rate is strong for a relationship-driven sales motion, but the base is small and the mix is concentrated — the top 3 co-ops account for 62% of ARR per the customer list. Two co-op managers confirmed live, daily use of the product in reference calls, which is a positive durability signal. The ARR figure is reported in USD but billed in local currency, so treat it as approximate pending the local-currency book.

Lattice charges co-ops a per-member annual subscription with tiered pricing by co-op size. Unit economics cannot be evaluated because no financial model was provided — this is the most important gap in the data room. Additionally, the company bills in MXN/COP but reports ARR in USD without hedging and re-prices only annually, so a 10–15% currency move would swing reported revenue materially. Partner should request the financial model, the local-currency ARR book, and the annual re-pricing history.

The dominant incumbent is Cropsifter, a legacy on-premise co-op management tool with ~150 customers that predates the smartphone era; Lattice positions as its mobile-first replacement. A smaller adjacent player, AgriTech Pro, focuses on single-farm management rather than co-ops. Lattice's defensibility rests on being embedded in the co-op's daily payment and intake workflows plus the founder's relationship moat, rather than on any structural network effect — a real but not impregnable position at this stage.

Base case: Lattice becomes the default co-op operating system in its two beachhead countries, expands across LatAm, and reaches a mid-eight-figure revenue business supporting a strategic acquisition by an agribusiness input supplier or a regional software roll-up. At the $12M entry and a $1M check for ~8%, a credible regional-leader outcome returns several multiples over a 6–8 year horizon. Downside: concentration bites (an anchor co-op churns), FX erodes reported growth, and the company stalls as a sub-scale regional tool — at which point the position is a partial loss or write-off. The partner judgment fields below capture the actual underwriting call.
[Partner to complete — base-case target multiple, upside thesis, downside floor, target ownership]

Three items before commitment. First, concentration: obtain contract terms, tenure, and switching costs for the top-3 co-ops (62% of ARR) and understand what happens to the plan if one leaves. Second, the missing financial model and cap table: request both — the model to underwrite unit economics and runway, the cap table to understand existing dilution before pricing the round. Third, FX: get the local-currency ARR book and understand the re-pricing cadence. Structural risks: a two-person team with no obvious go-to-market hire yet, and a long, relationship-driven sales cycle that is hard to accelerate with capital alone.

paragraphs.prose: Stellate is an edge-caching layer for SaaS application databases, founded in late 2023 by ex-Vercel and ex-Cloudflare engineers who built and shipped cache invalidation systems at production scale at their prior companies. The company is at $1.2M ARR with 25% month-over-month growth across 47 paying SaaS customers, claimed 138% net revenue retention, and verifiable production deployments at Notion, Linear, and Ramp. Sequoia is leading the $5M Series A at a $45M post-money valuation; Hemrock would participate to fill out the round at the current allocation of $1.25M for a 2.8% target ownership stake. The thesis is that edge data infrastructure is the next layer to consolidate after edge compute (Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge Functions), and the founding team has both the technical depth and the proximity to the buyer (SaaS infra engineering leads) to win it.

The single largest unresolved issue is a 60% discrepancy between the company-stated burn rate ($400K/mo in the deck) and the financial model's implied two-year average ($650K/mo derived from the $18M projected 2027 ARR and stated hiring plan). Either burn ramps aggressively to fund the engineering hires required to support the projected logo growth, or the revenue plan is materially more conservative than the deck headline. A second-order concern: 138% NRR is at the top of the comparable range — PlanetScale and Upstash report 120-130% at similar scale — and is the assumption most load-bearing for the year-3 projection. Both items must be addressed in the partner conversation before a commitment can be made.
[Partner to complete]

Stellate provides a database query caching layer that runs at edge points-of-presence and sits between the application server and the origin database. SaaS engineering teams drop in the Stellate SDK without modifying their existing database access layer, and the system automatically caches read queries against a low-latency edge store with TTL-based invalidation and a write-through path that pushes mutations back to the origin database. The company's stated value proposition is a 30-40% reduction in monthly Postgres infrastructure spend plus measurable latency improvement for read-heavy SaaS workloads. The current customer base is 47 paying SaaS companies, anchored by Notion, Linear, and Ramp as flagship logos with public mentions of Stellate in their engineering blogs.

The core product is a single npm package (`@stellate/cache`) plus a managed control plane. Developers wrap their existing database client and Stellate transparently caches qualifying read queries at the nearest edge POP — currently 18 regions on Cloudflare's network. The control-plane UI shows cache hit rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, and per-query cost savings; the data-room screenshots show real metrics from a customer with a 73% hit rate on a Postgres workload that previously cost $42K/month. Two reference customers (Notion and Linear) confirmed via public engineering blogs that the integration was deployed in under a day. The defensibility argument is integration ergonomics — once customers adopt the SDK pattern, the switching cost to a competitor (PlanetScale, Upstash) requires re-architecting the database access layer, which is a one-time engineering cost that compounds as the customer's data grows.

The edge data infrastructure category is roughly a $5B addressable spend today (third-party estimates from Battery and Bessemer market maps), growing at 35-40% annually as more SaaS applications adopt globally distributed architectures. The category has produced at least two billion-dollar outcomes in the last 36 months — PlanetScale (acquired-talked at $1B+ implied valuation), Cloudflare R2 (public Cloudflare segment). Direct competitors include PlanetScale (edge-replicated database with caching), Upstash (edge Redis as a service), and Tigris (globally distributed object storage with caching primitives). Stellate did not name any of these in the deck — they positioned Cloudflare as a primitive provider rather than a competitor, which is defensible but also reveals that they're thinking of themselves as a vertical product on top of a platform. Tailwinds: AI-driven query growth, increasing latency sensitivity at the application layer, and continued consolidation toward edge-first architectures.

Three-person founding team: Alex Chen (CEO), Priya Mehta (CTO), and Devon Rhodes (VP Engineering). Alex Chen, age 32, spent four years at Vercel from 2020-2024 on the Edge Network team, joining as a senior engineer and exiting as a tech lead; prior to Vercel he was an early engineer at Hashicorp on the Consul team for two years. Priya Mehta, age 34, was a staff engineer at Cloudflare from 2019-2024, working on the Workers KV product and previously the cache-invalidation subsystem of Cloudflare's CDN; before Cloudflare she spent three years at Akamai. Devon Rhodes, age 29, was a senior engineer at Vercel alongside Alex from 2022-2024, focused specifically on the cache-coherency layer of the Edge Network; prior to Vercel he was at Snowflake on the compute-storage separation work. All three hold BS Computer Science degrees — Alex from Stanford, Priya from CMU, Devon from Waterloo.

Founder-market fit is unusually direct: Alex's last project at Vercel was an internal cache-invalidation tool that Vercel decided not to productize, and Stellate is effectively the externalized version of that work with a different business model. Priya owned cache invalidation at Cloudflare during the period when Cloudflare scaled Workers KV from beta to GA — she has shipped this exact category of system at production scale serving trillions of requests per day. Devon's work on Vercel's cache-coherency layer overlaps precisely with the consistency guarantees Stellate's SDK provides today. Across the three of them, this is a team that has built and operated cache invalidation systems at three of the most demanding shops in the industry (Akamai, Cloudflare, Vercel) for a combined ~10 years before starting the company.

Public output is substantial for a team this size. Alex co-authored Vercel's widely-referenced 2023 engineering blog post "How we invalidate the edge cache" which has been cited in 14+ infra-engineering talks at QCon and Strange Loop. Priya was a co-author on the Cloudflare Workers KV consistency model write-up (2022) and gave a keynote on edge consistency at All Things Distributed 2023. Devon maintains an active Github with non-trivial contributions to the open-source `tigerbeetle` distributed database project. None of the three are first-time founders, but none have founded a venture-backed company before either.

Partner Q&A surfaced two notable reference data points. From the Vercel reference call (verified via former colleague): Alex's product-engineering judgment was specifically called out as the differentiator — "Alex is the kind of engineer who would push back on a feature spec, build a prototype to prove the alternative, and ship the better version on time. Most engineers do at most two of those three." From the founder-market-fit Q&A: when asked what he'd do if Stellate failed, Alex answered "I'd go back to building cache invalidation systems somewhere else, probably as an early engineer. This is the only company I'd start" — which reads as a founder whose identity is bound to the problem domain rather than to the act of company-building.
[Partner to complete — character assessment, founder-market fit judgment, and overall team score]

Company-stated traction is $1.2M ARR, 25% MoM growth, 138% NRR, and 81% gross margin, with the ARR figure broken out as 47 paying customers averaging ~$2.1K MRR per logo. Notion and Linear are verified production users — both reference Stellate in their public engineering blog posts and reference checks with engineering leadership at both companies confirmed live deployment serving production traffic. Ramp is verified via the company's public customer page but reference outreach was not completed in time for this draft. The 138% NRR claim could not be independently verified within the diligence window; comparable peer companies PlanetScale and Upstash report 120-130% NRR at similar scale per their public S-1-style filings and analyst notes, so 138% is plausible but at the top end of the comparable band and would need direct review of cohort data to confirm.

Subscription pricing structured as a base platform fee per workspace plus usage-based overage on cached query volume above the included monthly quota. Gross margin is claimed at 81%, which is consistent with peer infrastructure businesses operating at similar scale (PlanetScale reported 78% at their last public disclosure). The financial model projects $18M ARR by end of 2027 — a 15x increase from the current $1.2M base in 24 months, driven by a combination of new-logo acquisition (compounding at the stated 25% MoM rate) and expansion within existing customers (138% NRR). Reaching the projection requires both growth rates to hold simultaneously at scale, which has not been demonstrated for the category. Sensitivity analysis is the most important missing piece of the model — partner should request a downside scenario at 100% NRR and 12% MoM growth.

Direct competitors include PlanetScale (edge-replicated database with caching, $1B+ implied valuation, recent acquisition-talked status), Upstash (edge Redis as a service, last private round at $400M), and Tigris (globally distributed object storage with caching primitives, Series B). Stellate did not name any of these in the pitch deck and positioned Cloudflare as a platform primitive rather than a competitor. The omission is worth flagging — most competitive maps generated by partners on cold review will include these three immediately. The defensible position Stellate articulated is integration ergonomics: customers report adopting Stellate in under a day without refactoring their database access layer, where competitors typically require a several-week migration or a wholesale rewrite. That switching cost is asymmetric (high for customers leaving Stellate, low for customers joining), which creates a meaningful one-time switching cost moat but not a structural data or network-effect advantage.

Base-case scenario assumes Stellate executes the stated $18M ARR plan by end of 2027 and continues compounding into a $50-80M ARR business by year 7 (2030), which would be a credible Series C/D outcome. Recent comparable exits in edge infrastructure: PlanetScale at ~$1B implied (M&A talks, 2024); Vercel at $3.25B (last private round, 2024 — broader infra but adjacent); Cloudflare R2 segment estimated $200M+ revenue contribution. At $50-80M ARR, a strategic acquirer at 10-15x ARR multiple implies a $500M-$1.2B exit. At our entry valuation of $45M post and a $1.25M check for 2.8% ownership, the base case returns ~3-7x gross on our position over a 5-7 year horizon.

Upside scenario: Stellate becomes the default edge data layer for the next generation of SaaS, reaching $150-250M ARR by year 7 with continued 50%+ growth, supporting an IPO or strategic acquisition at $3-5B. Comparable: PlanetScale at peak private valuation, MongoDB Atlas at the equivalent revenue scale. At those outcomes our position returns 15-30x gross. Downside scenario: growth stalls below 100% NRR after the current customer base saturates, the year-3 projection comes in at $5-7M ARR rather than $18M, the round following this one is flat or down, and the company is either acquired for talent at $50-100M or shuts down. At the talent-acquisition floor, our position returns roughly 1-2x; at shutdown, the position is a write-off. Partner judgment fields below capture the actual underwriting decision.
[Partner to complete — base-case target multiple, upside thesis, downside floor, target ownership]

Three open questions before commitment. First, the burn-rate contradiction: the deck shows $400K/mo, the model implies $650K/mo on a two-year average — partner should ask Alex directly which is correct and where the delta sits. Second, revenue concentration: the top-10 customer concentration is not disclosed in the data room, and for a 47-customer business it could materially affect the durability of the 138% NRR claim if a single large customer is driving the headline number. Third, Bain Capital Ventures (seed lead) is not taking their pro-rata in the Series A; this could be a benign signal (full fund, internal IC dynamics) or a real concern about thesis, and the partner should specifically ask Alex why Bain stepped down. Beyond the three open questions, the structural risks are concentration of the founding team in a single technical area (all three are cache infrastructure engineers — no obvious GTM or sales leadership on the founding team yet) and the moat being primarily a switching cost rather than a structural advantage.

rubric.yaml_content:
# Memo Agent — Investment Memo Scoring Rubric
# Version: 0.1 (draft)
# Used by: Memo Drafting Agent (Stage 5 — scoring)
#
# Edit this file to change what gets scored, how, and by whom.
# Stable IDs (e.g. "market", "team") are referenced from qa_library.yaml —
# do not rename without updating cross-references there.

meta:
  version: "0.1"
  last_updated: "2026-05-06"
  owner: partners
  notes: |
    Draft v1. Partners to review the dimension list, scoring criteria,
    and the machine/partner-only assignments before week 1 sign-off.

scoring_scale:
  type: integer
  range: [1, 5]
  levels:
    1: "Significant concern. Disqualifying without strong offset."
    2: "Below bar. Real concerns that need to be addressed."
    3: "Acceptable. Meets baseline; not differentiated."
    4: "Strong. Clear positive signal."
    5: "Exceptional. Outlier in this dimension."

confidence_levels:
  - low      # Insufficient evidence or evidence quality is poor
  - medium   # Reasonable evidence with some gaps
  - high     # Strong, well-sourced evidence

scoring_modes:
  machine:
    description: "Agent produces a score with reasoning. Partner can override."
  partner_only:
    description: "Agent leaves blank. Partner scores based on judgment. Agent compiles supporting evidence into the section narrative but does not score."
  hybrid:
    description: "Agent drafts a tentative score with explicit caveats; partner finalizes."

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Dimensions
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

dimensions:

  - id: market
    name: "Market"
    mode: machine
    description: |
      Size, growth, and structural attractiveness of the market the
      company is addressing.
    sources:
      - data_room
      - market_research
    criteria:
      1: "Small or shrinking market; no clear path to venture-scale outcomes."
      2: "Moderate market with limited growth or significant headwinds."
      3: "Reasonable size and growth; not differentiated from many comparable opportunities."
      4: "Large, growing market with clear tailwinds; supports venture-scale outcomes."
      5: "Exceptional — large, fast-growing, structural shift creating a new category."
    signals_to_consider:
      - "TAM/SAM/SOM with credible third-party sources (not company-stated only)"
      - "Market growth rate and the underlying drivers"
      - "Regulatory tailwinds or headwinds"
      - "Recent funding activity in the space (signal of investor conviction)"
    flag_low_confidence_when:
      - "Only company-stated market size available; no independent verification"
      - "Market definition unclear or company is creating a new category"

  - id: product_technology
    name: "Product & Technology"
    mode: machine
    description: |
      Quality, defensibility, and differentiation of the product or
      underlying technology.
    sources:
      - data_room
      - market_research
      - founder_research
    criteria:
      1: "Undifferentiated; significant technical risk or commodity offering."
      2: "Product works but is incremental; thin technical moat."
      3: "Solid product, some differentiation; defensibility unclear."
      4: "Clearly differentiated product with credible technical edge."
      5: "Genuinely novel approach with deep technical moat or step-change in capability."
    signals_to_consider:
      - "What's hard about what they're building? Why hasn't it been done?"
      - "Technical talent depth (per founder/team research)"
      - "IP, proprietary data, or other non-replicable advantages"
      - "Customer reactions to the product itself, not just the pitch"
    flag_low_confidence_when:
      - "Product in early development; limited evidence of execution capability"

  - id: traction
    name: "Traction & Evidence"
    mode: machine
    description: |
      Concrete evidence of demand, usage, and momentum.
    sources:
      - data_room
      - market_research
    criteria:
      1: "No meaningful traction; traction claims unsupported."
      2: "Limited traction; growth slow or unclear."
      3: "Meaningful early traction; pace consistent with stage."
      4: "Strong traction relative to stage; momentum building."
      5: "Outlier traction; metrics in top decile for stage."
    signals_to_consider:
      - "ARR, growth rate, retention/churn (with assumptions surfaced)"
      - "Pipeline quality and sales cycle"
      - "Usage and engagement (not just signups)"
      - "Customer references — strong references over strong logos"
    flag_low_confidence_when:
      - "Pre-revenue or pre-product"
      - "Numbers from company materials only; no independent customer verification"

  - id: business_model
    name: "Business Model & Unit Economics"
    mode: machine
    description: |
      How the company makes money and whether the economics scale.
    sources:
      - data_room
      - market_research
    criteria:
      1: "Model unclear or fundamentally broken economics."
      2: "Model exists but unit economics weak or unproven."
      3: "Reasonable model; unit economics workable but not exceptional."
      4: "Strong unit economics with clear path to leverage at scale."
      5: "Exceptional economics — high gross margins, capital efficient, structural advantages."
    signals_to_consider:
      - "Gross margin and trajectory"
      - "CAC, LTV, payback period (and whether assumptions are credible)"
      - "Burn vs. runway vs. milestones to next round"
      - "Revenue concentration risk"
    flag_low_confidence_when:
      - "Financial model relies on aggressive assumptions not supported by current data"
      - "Insufficient operating history to assess economics"

  - id: competition_moat
    name: "Competitive Position & Moat"
    mode: machine
    description: |
      Who else is in the space, and what makes this company defensible.
    sources:
      - market_research
      - data_room
    criteria:
      1: "Crowded space; no clear differentiation; defensibility absent."
      2: "Competitive space; differentiation marginal."
      3: "Recognizable position in the market; moat plausible but unproven."
      4: "Clear competitive position; multiple credible moat sources."
      5: "Structural advantage — network effects, data moat, regulatory edge, or category-defining position."
    signals_to_consider:
      - "Direct competitors, adjacent competitors, incumbents"
      - "Competitors the company didn't mention (often more important than ones they did)"
      - "Switching costs, network effects, data advantages"
      - "Why this team wins this race"
    flag_low_confidence_when:
      - "Highly fragmented or rapidly evolving competitive landscape"
      - "Stealth competitors likely but unknowable"

  - id: team
    name: "Team"
    mode: partner_only
    description: |
      Founder-market fit, co-founder dynamics, character, motivation,
      and judgment. By policy this dimension is partner-scored only.
      Agent leaves the score blank and surfaces partner Q&A answers
      as supporting context in the team section narrative.
    sources:
      - partner_qa
      - crm_interactions
      - founder_research   # informational only — never scored by agent
    criteria:
      1: "Significant concerns about character, capability, or fit."
      2: "Real reservations; would need strong offsetting evidence."
      3: "Capable team; nothing exceptional but no red flags."
      4: "Strong team with clear founder-market fit and good dynamics."
      5: "Exceptional founders — judgment, character, drive, and fit are outliers."
    informed_by_qa_categories:
      - background_track_record
      - founder_market_fit
      - team_dynamics
      - domain_expertise
      - personality_character
    agent_behavior: |
      Do NOT produce a score for this dimension under any circumstance.
      Compile partner Q&A answers into the team section narrative.
      Flag any inconsistencies between partner answers and external
      founder research for partner attention.

  - id: deal_terms
    name: "Deal & Terms"
    mode: hybrid
    description: |
      Valuation, round structure, ownership target, and terms relative
      to the opportunity. Agent drafts based on data room and comps;
      partner finalizes.
    sources:
      - data_room
      - market_research
    criteria:
      1: "Terms inconsistent with opportunity; significant concerns."
      2: "Terms tight relative to comparables and risk profile."
      3: "Terms reasonable; not exceptional in either direction."
      4: "Attractive terms relative to opportunity and comparables."
      5: "Exceptional entry — terms significantly favorable given stage and traction."
    signals_to_consider:
      - "Valuation vs. comparables at stage"
      - "Round size relative to milestones"
      - "Ownership target and dilution path"
      - "Pro rata, board, information rights"
    flag_low_confidence_when:
      - "Terms not yet finalized"
      - "Limited comparable data for stage/sector"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Overall recommendation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

overall_recommendation:
  mode: partner_only
  description: |
    Per firm convention, the agent does not produce an overall
    recommendation. It surfaces dimension scores and confidence flags;
    partners decide.
  conventional_options:
    - "Strong yes — proceed to IC"
    - "Yes with conditions"
    - "Pass — track"
    - "Pass"

meta.notes:
Draft v1. Partners to review the dimension list, scoring criteria,
and the machine/partner-only assignments before week 1 sign-off.

dimensions.name: Market

criteria.1: Small or shrinking market; no clear path to venture-scale outcomes.
criteria.2: Moderate market with limited growth or significant headwinds.
criteria.3: Reasonable size and growth; not differentiated from many comparable opportunities.
criteria.4: Large, growing market with clear tailwinds; supports venture-scale outcomes.
criteria.5: Exceptional — large, fast-growing, structural shift creating a new category.

dimensions.description:
Size, growth, and structural attractiveness of the market the
company is addressing.
signals_to_consider: TAM/SAM/SOM with credible third-party sources (not company-stated only)
Market growth rate and the underlying drivers
Regulatory tailwinds or headwinds
Recent funding activity in the space (signal of investor conviction)
flag_low_confidence_when: Only company-stated market size available; no independent verification
Market definition unclear or company is creating a new category

dimensions.name: Product & Technology

criteria.1: Undifferentiated; significant technical risk or commodity offering.
criteria.2: Product works but is incremental; thin technical moat.
criteria.3: Solid product, some differentiation; defensibility unclear.
criteria.4: Clearly differentiated product with credible technical edge.
criteria.5: Genuinely novel approach with deep technical moat or step-change in capability.

dimensions.description:
Quality, defensibility, and differentiation of the product or
underlying technology.
signals_to_consider: What's hard about what they're building? Why hasn't it been done?
Technical talent depth (per founder/team research)
IP, proprietary data, or other non-replicable advantages
Customer reactions to the product itself, not just the pitch
flag_low_confidence_when: Product in early development; limited evidence of execution capability

dimensions.name: Traction & Evidence

criteria.1: No meaningful traction; traction claims unsupported.
criteria.2: Limited traction; growth slow or unclear.
criteria.3: Meaningful early traction; pace consistent with stage.
criteria.4: Strong traction relative to stage; momentum building.
criteria.5: Outlier traction; metrics in top decile for stage.

dimensions.description: Concrete evidence of demand, usage, and momentum.
signals_to_consider: ARR, growth rate, retention/churn (with assumptions surfaced)
Pipeline quality and sales cycle
Usage and engagement (not just signups)
Customer references — strong references over strong logos
flag_low_confidence_when: Numbers from company materials only; no independent customer verification

dimensions.name: Business Model & Unit Economics

criteria.1: Model unclear or fundamentally broken economics.
criteria.2: Model exists but unit economics weak or unproven.
criteria.3: Reasonable model; unit economics workable but not exceptional.
criteria.4: Strong unit economics with clear path to leverage at scale.
criteria.5: Exceptional economics — high gross margins, capital efficient, structural advantages.

dimensions.description: How the company makes money and whether the economics scale.
signals_to_consider: Gross margin and trajectory
CAC, LTV, payback period (and whether assumptions are credible)
Burn vs. runway vs. milestones to next round
Revenue concentration risk
flag_low_confidence_when: Financial model relies on aggressive assumptions not supported by current data
Insufficient operating history to assess economics

dimensions.name: Competitive Position & Moat

criteria.1: Crowded space; no clear differentiation; defensibility absent.
criteria.3: Recognizable position in the market; moat plausible but unproven.
criteria.4: Clear competitive position; multiple credible moat sources.
criteria.5: Structural advantage — network effects, data moat, regulatory edge, or category-defining position.

dimensions.description: Who else is in the space, and what makes this company defensible.
signals_to_consider: Direct competitors, adjacent competitors, incumbents
Competitors the company didn't mention (often more important than ones they did)
Switching costs, network effects, data advantages
Why this team wins this race
flag_low_confidence_when: Highly fragmented or rapidly evolving competitive landscape

dimensions.name: Team

criteria.1: Significant concerns about character, capability, or fit.
criteria.2: Real reservations; would need strong offsetting evidence.
criteria.3: Capable team; nothing exceptional but no red flags.
criteria.4: Strong team with clear founder-market fit and good dynamics.
criteria.5: Exceptional founders — judgment, character, drive, and fit are outliers.

dimensions.description:
Founder-market fit, co-founder dynamics, character, motivation,
and judgment. By policy this dimension is partner-scored only.
Agent leaves the score blank and surfaces partner Q&A answers
as supporting context in the team section narrative.
dimensions.agent_behavior:
Do NOT produce a score for this dimension under any circumstance.
Compile partner Q&A answers into the team section narrative.
Flag any inconsistencies between partner answers and external
founder research for partner attention.

dimensions.name: Deal & Terms

criteria.1: Terms inconsistent with opportunity; significant concerns.
criteria.2: Terms tight relative to comparables and risk profile.
criteria.3: Terms reasonable; not exceptional in either direction.
criteria.4: Attractive terms relative to opportunity and comparables.
criteria.5: Exceptional entry — terms significantly favorable given stage and traction.

signals_to_consider: Valuation vs. comparables at stage
Round size relative to milestones
Ownership target and dilution path
Pro rata, board, information rights

hybrid.description: Agent drafts a tentative score with explicit caveats; partner finalizes.

machine.description: Agent produces a score with reasoning. Partner can override.

partner_only.description: Agent leaves blank. Partner scores based on judgment. Agent compiles supporting evidence into the section narrative but does not score.

levels.1: Significant concern. Disqualifying without strong offset.
levels.2: Below bar. Real concerns that need to be addressed.

qa_library.yaml_content:
# Memo Agent — Founder Q&A Library
# Version: 0.1 (draft)
# Used by: Memo Drafting Agent (Stage 3 — partner Q&A)
#
# Each question has a stable ID. When removing or rephrasing,
# do NOT renumber — the ID is the unit of measurement for tracking
# which questions surface real signal over time.
#
# `feeds_dimensions` cross-references rubric.yaml dimension IDs.

meta:
  version: "0.1"
  last_updated: "2026-05-06"
  owner: partners
  notes: |
    Draft v1 derived from the build spec. Partners to refine phrasing,
    add or remove questions based on what surfaces real insight in practice.

batching_rules:
  questions_per_batch: { min: 4, max: 6 }
  ordering: |
    Start with background/track record (lower stakes, builds rhythm).
    Then founder-market fit, team dynamics, domain expertise.
    Save personality/character for the last batch — by then the partner
    has surfaced enough context that those questions land sharper.
  spacing: |
    Wait for partner answers before sending the next batch. Never send
    all batches at once. If a partner skips more than 2 questions in
    a batch, note it and move on rather than pushing.

skip_logic:
  global_rules:
    - "If CRM interaction notes already answer the question, reference the note and ask a follow-up instead of the original question."
    - "If a prior answer in this session covered the ground, skip and note as covered."
    - "If the data room contains content that answers the question (e.g., founder bio), reference it and ask a verification or follow-up."

sensitivity_levels:
  standard: "Ask directly."
  high: |
    Frame thoughtfully. These questions touch on character, integrity,
    or red flags. Ask in a way that invites honest reflection, not defensiveness.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Categories (ordered)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

categories:
  - { id: background_track_record, name: "Background, track record, references", order: 1 }
  - { id: founder_market_fit,      name: "Founder-market fit and motivation",    order: 2 }
  - { id: team_dynamics,           name: "Team dynamics and co-founder relationship", order: 3 }
  - { id: domain_expertise,        name: "Domain expertise and unfair advantages", order: 4 }
  - { id: personality_character,   name: "Personality and character",            order: 5 }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Questions
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

questions:

  # --- Background, track record, references ---
  - id: bg_001
    category: background_track_record
    prompt: "What's the strongest signal you got from references?"
    intent: "Surface the single most important reference takeaway, positive or negative."
    kind: open_text
    feeds_dimensions: [team]
    sensitivity: standard
    skip_if_covered_in: [crm_notes]

  - id: bg_002
    category: background_track_record
    prompt: "Have you verified the major claims in their background — degrees, prior roles, exits?"
    intent: "Catch resume inflation early. Distinguishes verified from assumed."
    kind: yes_no_with_context
    feeds_dimensions: [team]
    sensitivity: standard

  - id: bg_003
    category: background_track_record
    prompt: "Is there anyone in your network who's worked with them before? What did they say?"
    intent: "Backchannel references are often more honest than provided ones."
    kind: open_text
    feeds_dimensions: [team]
    sensitivity: standard
    reference_signal_in_crm: "Check connection mapping in your CRM for shared connections."

  - id: bg_004
    category: background_track_record
    prompt: "Are there gaps or transitions in their history they didn't address? Did you ask?"
    intent: "Unexplained gaps are not necessarily concerning, but unexplored ones are."
    kind: open_text
    feeds_dimensions: [team]
    sensitivity: high

  # --- Founder-market fit and motivation ---
  - id: fmf_001
    category: founder_market_fit
    prompt: "Why this problem? Did their answer go beyond surface-level?"
    intent: "Depth of the 'why now, why me' story is a strong predictor of resilience."
    kind: open_text
    feeds_dimensions: [team]
    sensitivity: standard

  - id: fmf_002
    category: founder_market_fit
    prompt: "How long have they been thinking about this space — months, years, a decade?"
    intent: "Distinguish people pulled to a problem from people picking a market."
    kind: open_text
    feeds_dimensions: [team]
    sensitivity: standard

  - id: fmf_003
    category: founder_market_fit
    prompt: "What would they do if this didn't work?"
    intent: "Tests whether the problem owns them or they're problem-shopping."
    kind: open_text
    feeds_dimensions: [team]
    sensitivity: standard

  - id: fmf_004
    category: founder_market_fit
    prompt: "Is the motivation pulling them forward, or are they pushing themselves?"
    intent: "Pull is sustainable through hard years; push usually isn't."
    kind: open_text
    feeds_dimensions: [team]
    sensitivity: high

  # --- Team dynamics ---
  - id: td_001
    category: team_dynamics
    prompt: "How long have the co-founders known each other, and in what context?"
    intent: "Length and depth of relationship before founding predicts dynamics under stress."
    kind: open_text
    feeds_dimensions: [team]
    sensitivity: standard
    skip_if_covered_in: [data_room, crm_notes]

  - id: td_002
    category: team_dynamics
    prompt: "Have they been through a hard moment together? What happened?"
    intent: "Untested partnerships often crack on first real stress."
    kind: open_text
    feeds_dimensions: [team]
    sensitivity: standard

  - id: td_003
    category: team_dynamics
    prompt: "Who's clearly the CEO? Is there role clarity, or is it ambiguous?"
    intent: "Ambiguous leadership often shows up later as cap table disputes."
    kind: open_text
    feeds_dimensions: [team]
    sensitivity: standard

  - id: td_004
    category: team_dynamics
    prompt: "If you had to bet on one of them solo, who would it be and why?"
    intent: "Forces a real comparison; the answer often reveals who's actually driving."
    kind: open_text
    feeds_dimensions: [team]
    sensitivity: high

  - id: td_005
    category: team_dynamics
    prompt: "Did you sense any tension in your meetings — interruptions, contradictions, body language?"
    intent: "Tension under low-stakes pitch usually means worse tension under real stress."
    kind: open_text
    feeds_dimensions: [team]
    sensitivity: high

  # --- Domain expertise ---
  - id: de_001
    category: domain_expertise
    prompt: "What do they know that others in this space don't?"
    intent: "Surface the actual edge — not credentials, but proprietary insight."
    kind: open_text
    feeds_dimensions: [team, product_technology]
    sensitivity: standard

  - id: de_002
    category: domain_expertise
    prompt: "What's their unfair access — customers, talent, capital, distribution?"
    intent: "Concrete advantages, not theoretical ones."
    kind: open_text
    feeds_dimensions: [team, competition_moat]
    sensitivity: standard

  - id: de_003
    category: domain_expertise
    prompt: "Have they shipped before? Hired before? Sold before?"
    intent: "Operating range matters more than pedigree."
    kind: open_text
    feeds_dimensions: [team]
    sensitivity: standard
    skip_if_covered_in: [founder_research]

  - id: de_004
    category: domain_expertise
    prompt: "If a smart competitor entered tomorrow with similar funding, what would these founders have that the competitor wouldn't?"
    intent: "Identifies founder-specific moat vs. transferable advantages."
    kind: open_text
    feeds_dimensions: [team, competition_moat]
    sensitivity: standard

  # --- Personality and character ---
  - id: pc_001
    category: personality_character
    prompt: "How did they handle hard questions in your meetings — defensive, curious, honest?"
    intent: "Reaction to challenge is one of the most predictive single signals."
    kind: open_text
    feeds_dimensions: [team]
    sensitivity: high

  - id: pc_002
    category: personality_character
    prompt: "Did they tell you about a recent failure unprompted?"
    intent: "Self-disclosed failure usually correlates with self-awareness; absence is a flag."
    kind: yes_no_with_context
    feeds_dimensions: [team]
    sensitivity: high

  - id: pc_003
    category: personality_character
    prompt: "How do they talk about their team — credit-taking or credit-giving?"
    intent: "Predicts ability to attract and keep talent."
    kind: open_text
    feeds_dimensions: [team]
    sensitivity: high

  - id: pc_004
    category: personality_character
    prompt: "How do they talk about competitors — dismissive, respectful, learning-from?"
    intent: "Dismissiveness toward competitors is a consistent negative signal."
    kind: open_text
    feeds_dimensions: [team, competition_moat]
    sensitivity: high

  - id: pc_005
    category: personality_character
    prompt: "Coachability: did they update on anything you said, or just defend their view?"
    intent: "Updating in real time is a strong positive; pure defense is concerning."
    kind: open_text
    feeds_dimensions: [team]
    sensitivity: high

  - id: pc_006
    category: personality_character
    prompt: "Did anything they said turn out not to match what you found later?"
    intent: "Integrity gaps that surface during diligence usually grow, not shrink."
    kind: yes_no_with_context
    feeds_dimensions: [team]
    sensitivity: high

  - id: pc_007
    category: personality_character
    prompt: "What's your gut on whether you'd want to work with this person for 7–10 years through hard things?"
    intent: "The single most important question. Trust the answer."
    kind: open_text
    feeds_dimensions: [team]
    sensitivity: high

  - id: pc_008
    category: personality_character
    prompt: "Anything that nagged at you that you can't quite articulate?"
    intent: "Pattern-recognition without clear cause is often valid signal. Surface it before it gets rationalized away."
    kind: open_text
    feeds_dimensions: [team]
    sensitivity: high

data_room_ingestion.yaml_content:
# Memo Agent — Data Room Ingestion Schema
# Version: 0.1 (draft)
# Used by: Memo Drafting Agent (Stage 1 — ingestion)
#
# Defines: how each document in a Google Drive data room gets parsed
# into structured claims, what document types we recognize, what we
# expect to find (so we can flag gaps), and how financial models get
# special treatment so company projections don't leak in as facts.

meta:
  version: "0.1"
  last_updated: "2026-05-06"
  owner: vendor   # Technical schema; partners review but don't typically edit.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Provenance — every claim from the data room carries this by default
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

provenance_default:
  source_type: company_stated
  rationale: |
    Every claim extracted from the data room is treated as
    "company-stated" — the company has asserted it; it has NOT been
    independently verified. The agent must never elevate a
    company-stated claim to a fact in the memo. Verification belongs
    to Stage 2 (external research) and Stage 3 (partner Q&A). This
    is the single most important guardrail in this schema.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Document types
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

document_types:
  - id: pitch_deck
    name: "Pitch deck"
    typical_formats: [pdf, pptx, gslides]
    typical_content: [problem, solution, market, traction, team, ask]
    extraction_priority: high

  - id: financial_model
    name: "Financial model / projections"
    typical_formats: [xlsx, gsheets]
    typical_content: [historical_metrics, projections, assumptions, unit_economics]
    extraction_priority: high
    special_handling: financial_extraction   # see below

  - id: cap_table
    name: "Cap table"
    typical_formats: [xlsx, gsheets, pdf]
    typical_content: [ownership, option_pool, prior_rounds, preferences]
    extraction_priority: high

  - id: founder_bios
    name: "Founder bios / resumes"
    typical_formats: [pdf, docx]
    typical_content: [education, prior_roles, exits, publications]
    extraction_priority: high

  - id: customer_reference
    name: "Customer reference / case study"
    typical_formats: [pdf, docx, gdocs, video, audio]
    typical_content: [customer_name, use_case, outcomes, willingness_to_reference]
    extraction_priority: high

  - id: product_demo
    name: "Product demo"
    typical_formats: [video, mp4, mov]
    typical_content: [product_walkthrough, ux, capabilities]
    extraction_priority: medium
    note: "Transcribe audio; extract feature list and key claims."

  - id: technical_doc
    name: "Technical architecture / spec"
    typical_formats: [pdf, docx, gdocs, md]
    typical_content: [architecture, stack, ip, moat_claims]
    extraction_priority: medium

  - id: market_analysis_internal
    name: "Company-prepared market analysis"
    typical_formats: [pdf, docx, gdocs, pptx]
    typical_content: [tam_sam_som, competitors, trends]
    extraction_priority: medium
    note: |
      Treat with extra skepticism. Company-prepared analyses tend to be
      selectively sourced. Flag every claim for verification in Stage 2.

  - id: prior_round_terms
    name: "Prior round terms / SAFE / agreements"
    typical_formats: [pdf, docx]
    typical_content: [valuation, investors, rights, preferences]
    extraction_priority: high

  - id: hiring_plan
    name: "Hiring plan"
    typical_formats: [xlsx, gsheets, pdf]
    typical_content: [roles, timing, comp_bands]
    extraction_priority: medium

  - id: roadmap
    name: "Product roadmap"
    typical_formats: [pdf, pptx, gsheets]
    typical_content: [milestones, timing, features]
    extraction_priority: medium

  - id: whiteboard_or_sketch
    name: "Whiteboard photo / strategy sketch"
    typical_formats: [jpg, png, heic]
    typical_content: [informal_diagrams, strategy_notes]
    extraction_priority: low
    note: "OCR plus visual interpretation. Often partial; flag low confidence."

  - id: press_coverage
    name: "Press coverage / clips"
    typical_formats: [pdf, link, gdocs]
    typical_content: [headlines, publication, date, tone]
    extraction_priority: low
    note: "Useful as signal, not as fact."

  - id: other
    name: "Other / unclassified"
    typical_formats: [any]
    extraction_priority: low
    note: "Catch-all. Surface for partner review rather than guessing."

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Expected documents — drives gap analysis
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

expected_documents:
  description: |
    What we'd typically expect to find in a complete data room. Items
    not present become entries in the gap_analysis output. Absence
    isn't necessarily a flag — but it should always be visible.
  expected:
    - { id: pitch_deck,         criticality: required }
    - { id: financial_model,    criticality: required }
    - { id: cap_table,          criticality: required }
    - { id: founder_bios,       criticality: required }
    - { id: customer_reference, criticality: expected }
    - { id: product_demo,       criticality: expected }
    - { id: prior_round_terms,  criticality: expected }
    - { id: hiring_plan,        criticality: optional }
    - { id: roadmap,            criticality: optional }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Per-document extraction format
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

document_record:
  fields:
    - { name: id,                  type: string,   required: true,  note: "Stable per-data-room ID." }
    - { name: file_name,           type: string,   required: true }
    - { name: file_format,         type: string,   required: true,  note: "pdf, xlsx, gslides, mp4, etc." }
    - { name: drive_path,          type: string,   required: true }
    - { name: drive_file_id,       type: string,   required: true,  note: "Google Drive file ID for traceability." }
    - { name: detected_type,       type: string,   required: true,  note: "ID from document_types." }
    - { name: type_confidence,     type: enum,     required: true,  values: [low, medium, high] }
    - { name: document_date,       type: date,     required: false, note: "Author date if found; else file modified date." }
    - { name: page_or_slide_count, type: integer,  required: false }
    - { name: parse_status,        type: enum,     required: true,  values: [parsed, partial, failed, skipped] }
    - { name: parse_notes,         type: string,   required: false, note: "Why partial/failed (scanned, password-protected, etc.)." }
    - { name: summary,             type: string,   required: true,  note: "1–3 sentence summary of the document's purpose and content." }
    - { name: claims,              type: list,     required: false, note: "List of claim_record entries — see below." }
    - { name: financial_extract,   type: object,   required: false, note: "Only for financial_model; see financial_extraction." }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Claim record — every meaningful assertion extracted from the data room
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

claim_record:
  description: |
    A discrete assertion extracted from a document. Each claim is
    tagged with provenance, the section of the memo it likely feeds,
    and a verification status the research stage will update.
  fields:
    - { name: id,                  type: string,  required: true,  note: "Stable claim ID, e.g. 'pitch_deck_001_claim_03'." }
    - { name: text,                type: string,  required: true,  note: "The claim, phrased neutrally — strip marketing voice." }
    - { name: claim_type,          type: enum,    required: true,  values: [metric, market_size, competitive_position, customer_evidence, team_credential, product_capability, financial_projection, other] }
    - { name: source_document_id,  type: string,  required: true }
    - { name: source_location,     type: string,  required: false, note: "Page, slide, cell — wherever the claim lives." }
    - { name: source_type,         type: enum,    required: true,  values: [company_stated, third_party_cited_by_company, customer_quoted_by_company] }
    - { name: feeds_memo_section,  type: list,    required: true,  note: "Memo sections this claim is likely relevant to." }
    - { name: verification_status, type: enum,    required: true,  values: [unverified, verification_attempted, verified, contradicted, unverifiable] }
    - { name: verification_notes,  type: string,  required: false, note: "How and where it was verified, or why not." }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Financial model — special handling
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

financial_extraction:
  rationale: |
    Financial models are dense with numbers that look like facts. They
    are not. Every projection rests on assumptions, and the assumptions
    are where the actual judgment lives. The agent extracts both, links
    each metric to its driving assumptions, and surfaces aggressiveness
    versus historical actuals where comparison is possible. The agent
    does NOT critique the model — it makes the assumption layer visible
    so the partner can.

  metrics_to_extract:
    - { id: arr,             name: "ARR",                   units: currency, historical: required, projected: required }
    - { id: arr_growth,      name: "ARR growth rate",       units: percent,  historical: required, projected: required }
    - { id: gross_margin,    name: "Gross margin",          units: percent,  historical: required, projected: required }
    - { id: net_margin,      name: "Net margin",            units: percent,  historical: optional, projected: optional }
    - { id: burn,            name: "Net burn (monthly)",    units: currency, historical: required, projected: required }
    - { id: runway,          name: "Runway (months)",       units: months,   historical: required, projected: required }
    - { id: cac,             name: "CAC",                   units: currency, historical: optional, projected: optional }
    - { id: ltv,             name: "LTV",                   units: currency, historical: optional, projected: optional }
    - { id: ltv_cac,         name: "LTV:CAC ratio",         units: ratio,    historical: optional, projected: optional }
    - { id: payback_months,  name: "CAC payback (months)",  units: months,   historical: optional, projected: optional }
    - { id: nrr,             name: "Net revenue retention", units: percent,  historical: optional, projected: optional }
    - { id: gross_retention, name: "Gross retention",       units: percent,  historical: optional, projected: optional }
    - { id: headcount,       name: "Headcount",             units: count,    historical: required, projected: required }

  metric_record:
    fields:
      - { name: metric_id,           type: string }
      - { name: value,               type: number_or_range }
      - { name: period,              type: string,   note: "e.g., 'FY2025', 'Q3 2025', 'projected EOY 2027'." }
      - { name: is_projection,       type: boolean }
      - { name: cell_reference,      type: string,   note: "Sheet name + cell, for traceability." }
      - { name: driving_assumptions, type: list,     note: "List of assumption_record IDs this metric depends on." }

  assumption_record:
    fields:
      - { name: id,                     type: string }
      - { name: text,                   type: string,  note: "The assumption, stated plainly. e.g., 'Sales rep ramps to full quota in 4 months.'" }
      - { name: cell_reference,         type: string }
      - { name: assumption_type,        type: enum,    values: [growth_rate, conversion_rate, churn_rate, headcount_plan, pricing, cogs, opex_ratio, other] }
      - { name: aggressiveness,         type: enum,    values: [conservative, in_line_with_history, optimistic, aggressive, unmarked], note: "Compared to historical actuals where available; 'unmarked' when no historical comparison possible." }
      - { name: partner_attention_flag, type: boolean, note: "True when the assumption is materially more aggressive than historical actuals." }

  rules:
    - "Never quote a projected number without surfacing its driving assumptions in the memo or appendix."
    - "Mark every projection as 'projected' in the memo; do not blur the historical/projected line."
    - "Flag assumptions materially more aggressive than historical actuals; do not editorialize on whether they are achievable."
    - "The agent does not score the model. It surfaces structure for partner judgment."

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Gap analysis — what's expected but missing
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

gap_analysis:
  description: |
    Run after all documents are ingested. Compare detected types
    against `expected_documents`. Output the list of expected items
    that were not found, with criticality and implication.
  output_record:
    fields:
      - { name: missing_type,            type: string }
      - { name: criticality,             type: enum,   values: [required, expected, optional] }
      - { name: implication,             type: string, note: "What this absence means for the memo (e.g., 'Without a financial model, projections section will be partner-driven only.')." }
      - { name: partner_recommendation,  type: string, note: "What the agent recommends asking the company for." }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Ingestion output — the artifact handed to Stage 2 (research) and Stage 4 (drafting)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

ingestion_output:
  fields:
    - { name: data_room_id,         type: string,    required: true }
    - { name: ingestion_date,       type: datetime,  required: true }
    - { name: documents,            type: list,      required: true,  note: "List of document_record entries." }
    - { name: claims,               type: list,      required: true,  note: "Flattened list of all claim_record entries across documents." }
    - { name: financial_summary,    type: object,    required: false, note: "Aggregated financial_extraction across the model(s)." }
    - { name: gaps,                 type: list,      required: true,  note: "List of gap_analysis entries." }
    - { name: partner_review_notes, type: string,    required: false, note: "Free text for the agent's overall observations — what surprised it, what's missing, what looked unusual." }

research_dossier.yaml_content:
# Memo Agent — External Research Dossier Schema
# Version: 0.1 (draft)
# Used by: Memo Drafting Agent (Stage 2 — external research)
#
# Symmetric partner to data_room_ingestion.yaml. Where that captures
# what the COMPANY says, this captures what the WORLD says — with
# the same provenance / confidence / feeds-section discipline.
#
# Findings link back to claims in the ingestion output by claim ID,
# updating verification_status. The two schemas together fully define
# the input to memo drafting (Stage 4).

meta:
  version: "0.1"
  last_updated: "2026-05-06"
  owner: vendor
  notes: |
    Per spec constraint: NO LinkedIn scraping. Founder research draws
    from the alternative source taxonomy below. Per spec policy: the
    agent compiles research material on founders but does NOT score
    the team dimension — that remains partner-only (see rubric.yaml).

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Categories of research
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

research_categories:
  - id: market
    name: "Market validation"
    description: "Independent verification of market size, growth, and dynamics claimed by the company."
    feeds_dimensions: [market]

  - id: competitive
    name: "Competitive landscape"
    description: "Direct, adjacent, and incumbent competitors. Includes competitors the company did not mention — usually the most valuable output of this category."
    feeds_dimensions: [competition_moat, product_technology]

  - id: founder_team
    name: "Founder and team research"
    description: "Background, prior work, public statements, technical output. Compiled for partner judgment; never scored by the agent."
    feeds_dimensions: [team]   # Partner-only dimension. Agent surfaces material; partner scores.

  - id: customer_validation
    name: "Customer and demand validation"
    description: "Independent signals of customer demand or product reception — reviews, forums, public references."
    feeds_dimensions: [traction, product_technology]

  - id: regulatory
    name: "Regulatory and policy environment"
    description: "Tailwinds, headwinds, pending legislation, compliance requirements."
    feeds_dimensions: [market, business_model]

  - id: technical_validation
    name: "Technical validation"
    description: "Independent assessment of technical claims — papers, benchmarks, engineering output."
    feeds_dimensions: [product_technology, competition_moat]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Source types and quality tiers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Source quality drives confidence. The agent must record source type
# alongside every finding. "I read it on the internet" is not a finding.

source_quality_tiers:
  tier_1_authoritative:
    description: "Primary or near-primary sources with strong editorial or methodological standards."
    examples:
      - "Government data (Census, BLS, SEC filings, regulatory filings)"
      - "Peer-reviewed research"
      - "Major analyst firms with disclosed methodology (Gartner, Forrester, IDC)"
      - "Industry associations with published methodology"
      - "Court records, patent filings"
    default_confidence: high

  tier_2_credible:
    description: "Established journalism and research with editorial standards but secondary."
    examples:
      - "Established business journalism (FT, WSJ, Bloomberg, Reuters, The Information)"
      - "Vertical trade press with reputation"
      - "Crunchbase, PitchBook (for funding/round data)"
      - "Company press releases and SEC filings (for that company's own facts)"
    default_confidence: medium_to_high

  tier_3_signal:
    description: "Useful as signal of sentiment or surface-level fact; not relied on alone for material claims."
    examples:
      - "Company website and marketing materials (third-party companies — not the target company)"
      - "Podcast interviews, conference talks"
      - "Founder personal blogs, Substacks"
      - "Product Hunt, G2, Capterra reviews (signal, not statistic)"
      - "GitHub repositories and release history"
    default_confidence: medium

  tier_4_weak:
    description: "Use only with corroboration. Never the sole source for a material claim."
    examples:
      - "Reddit, Hacker News, Twitter/X threads"
      - "Glassdoor reviews"
      - "Anonymous forum posts"
      - "Aggregator and SEO-optimized listicles"
    default_confidence: low

  tier_excluded:
    description: "Never used."
    examples:
      - "LinkedIn scraping (per spec)"
      - "Sites that require authentication or bypass paywalls"
      - "Dark social, leaked private data"
      - "Sites flagged for misinformation or extremism"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Finding record — the unit of external research
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

finding_record:
  description: "A discrete piece of external information the agent has gathered."
  fields:
    - { name: id,                        type: string,  required: true,  note: "Stable finding ID, e.g. 'finding_market_001'." }
    - { name: category,                  type: string,  required: true,  note: "ID from research_categories." }
    - { name: text,                      type: string,  required: true,  note: "The finding, phrased neutrally." }
    - { name: finding_type,              type: enum,    required: true,  values: [fact, signal, opinion, datapoint, contradiction], note: "fact = independently established; signal = directional but not conclusive; opinion = third-party interpretation; datapoint = a specific number; contradiction = directly contradicts a company claim." }
    - { name: source_url,                type: url,     required: true,  note: "Direct URL. If multiple sources, the primary." }
    - { name: source_publisher,          type: string,  required: true,  note: "e.g., 'Bloomberg', 'SEC EDGAR', 'GitHub'." }
    - { name: source_date,               type: date,    required: false, note: "Publication date. Recency matters; flag if >18 months old." }
    - { name: source_quality_tier,       type: enum,    required: true,  values: [tier_1_authoritative, tier_2_credible, tier_3_signal, tier_4_weak] }
    - { name: corroborating_sources,     type: list,    required: false, note: "Additional URLs supporting the same finding. Multi-source raises confidence." }
    - { name: confidence,                type: enum,    required: true,  values: [low, medium, high] }
    - { name: confidence_rationale,      type: string,  required: false, note: "Why this confidence level — source tier, corroboration, recency, methodology." }
    - { name: feeds_memo_section,        type: list,    required: true,  note: "Memo sections this finding is relevant to." }
    - { name: relates_to_claim_id,       type: string,  required: false, note: "If this finding bears on a specific data-room claim, reference it here." }
    - { name: relationship_to_claim,     type: enum,    required: false, values: [confirms, partially_confirms, contradicts, contextualizes, unrelated], note: "How this finding relates to the company-stated claim." }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contradiction record — surfaced separately because they matter most
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

contradiction_record:
  rationale: |
    When external evidence contradicts a company-stated claim, that's
    the highest-value output of the research stage. Partners need
    these surfaced clearly, not buried in a flat list of findings.
    Every contradiction also writes back to the originating claim's
    verification_status (set to 'contradicted' in the ingestion
    output).
  fields:
    - { name: id,                  type: string,  required: true }
    - { name: company_claim_id,    type: string,  required: true,  note: "Claim ID from data_room_ingestion." }
    - { name: company_claim_text,  type: string,  required: true,  note: "Restated for partner readability." }
    - { name: contradicting_finding_ids, type: list, required: true }
    - { name: nature,              type: enum,    required: true,  values: [factual, definitional, methodological, temporal, scope], note: "factual = numbers don't match; definitional = different definition of the same term; methodological = different measurement approach; temporal = the claim was true at one time but isn't now; scope = the claim is true for a subset but stated as universal." }
    - { name: severity,            type: enum,    required: true,  values: [minor, moderate, material], note: "How much it should affect partner judgment." }
    - { name: agent_notes,         type: string,  required: false, note: "Neutral framing of the discrepancy. Do not editorialize on intent." }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Founder & team research — special handling
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

founder_research_special_handling:
  rationale: |
    Constraints: no LinkedIn scraping; team dimension is partner-only;
    the agent compiles material but does not interpret character. This
    section defines what's in-scope, what's out-of-scope, and the
    alternative source taxonomy that fills the gap LinkedIn would
    otherwise occupy.

  in_scope:
    - "Public professional history from company websites, press, official bios"
    - "Published work: papers, patents, talks, books, podcasts"
    - "Open source contributions (GitHub, package registries)"
    - "Public statements: interviews, panel appearances, public letters"
    - "Verifiable affiliations: prior companies, advisor roles, board seats"
    - "Press mentions including coverage of prior ventures, exits, lawsuits"
    - "Court records (subject to ethical and legal considerations)"
    - "Educational credentials where publicly verified"

  out_of_scope:
    - "LinkedIn scraping (per spec constraint)"
    - "Personal social media used for personal life (non-professional content)"
    - "Speculation about personal relationships, family, or health"
    - "Inference from photos, lifestyle, or appearance"
    - "Anonymous accusations without corroboration"
    - "Any character interpretation — the agent surfaces material; the partner interprets"

  alternative_source_taxonomy:
    primary_sources:
      - { id: company_history,       name: "Prior company websites and About pages", priority: high }
      - { id: press_coverage,        name: "Press coverage of prior roles and exits", priority: high }
      - { id: government_filings,    name: "SEC, Companies House, regulatory filings", priority: high, note: "For director histories and prior ventures." }
      - { id: court_records,         name: "Public court records",                     priority: medium, note: "Use cautiously; pending matters are not findings." }
      - { id: patent_filings,        name: "USPTO, EPO, WIPO",                         priority: medium }
      - { id: academic_publications, name: "Google Scholar, arXiv, peer-reviewed work", priority: high, note: "For technical founders." }
      - { id: open_source,           name: "GitHub, package registries",                priority: high, note: "For technical founders — code is the strongest available signal." }
      - { id: conference_talks,      name: "YouTube talks, conference recordings",      priority: medium }
      - { id: podcast_interviews,    name: "Podcast appearances",                       priority: medium, note: "Often more candid than written press." }
      - { id: long_form_interviews,  name: "Magazine profiles, deep-dive articles",     priority: medium }
      - { id: founder_writing,       name: "Personal blogs, Substacks, op-eds",         priority: medium, note: "Distinguish between personal voice and ghostwritten content." }

    backchannel_signals:
      description: "Your CRM's connection mapping surfaces who in the partner network has worked with these founders. The agent identifies the connections; the partner does the actual outreach. Backchannel content is never reported in the dossier as a finding — it is collected by the partner and entered through Q&A."
      agent_action: "Surface the connection list with prior affiliations. Do not contact, do not summarize what others might say."

  output_constraints:
    - "Compile material. Do not interpret character."
    - "Direct quotes only when source is reliable; paraphrase otherwise."
    - "Flag inconsistencies between data room founder bios and external sources."
    - "Flag prior ventures the company did not mention."
    - "Never state or imply a personal characteristic that isn't directly evidenced."

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Competitive research — special handling
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

competitive_research_special_handling:
  rationale: |
    The most valuable output of competitive research is usually the
    competitors the company did NOT mention. Companies systematically
    under-represent competition in pitch materials. This section
    forces the agent to look beyond the company-supplied list.

  required_outputs:
    - { id: company_named_competitors,    name: "Competitors named by the company", required: true }
    - { id: company_unnamed_competitors,  name: "Competitors NOT named by the company but operating in the same space", required: true, note: "Highest-value output of this stage." }
    - { id: adjacent_competitors,         name: "Adjacent players who could enter", required: true }
    - { id: incumbent_competitors,        name: "Incumbents who already serve this need (often with worse products)", required: true }
    - { id: build_vs_buy_alternatives,    name: "What customers do today instead of buying anything", required: false, note: "Sometimes 'a spreadsheet' is the real competitor." }

  per_competitor_record:
    fields:
      - { name: id,                    type: string }
      - { name: name,                  type: string }
      - { name: category,              type: enum,    values: [direct, adjacent, incumbent, alternative] }
      - { name: company_mentioned,     type: boolean, note: "Did the company name them in the data room?" }
      - { name: positioning_summary,   type: string,  note: "1–2 sentence neutral description of what they do." }
      - { name: stage,                 type: enum,    values: [seed, series_a, series_b, growth, public, private_mature, unknown] }
      - { name: most_recent_funding,   type: object,  required: false, note: "Round, amount, date, lead — when known." }
      - { name: differentiation_vs_target, type: string, note: "How target company is positioned differently. Neutral framing." }
      - { name: source_urls,           type: list }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Research output — handed to Stage 4 (drafting)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

research_output:
  fields:
    - { name: dossier_id,        type: string,    required: true }
    - { name: research_date,     type: datetime,  required: true }
    - { name: findings,          type: list,      required: true,  note: "All finding_record entries." }
    - { name: contradictions,    type: list,      required: true,  note: "All contradiction_record entries." }
    - { name: competitive_map,   type: object,    required: true,  note: "Output of competitive_research_special_handling." }
    - { name: founder_dossiers,  type: list,      required: true,  note: "One per founder; compiled material only." }
    - { name: claim_verifications, type: list,    required: true,  note: "Updates to data_room_ingestion claim verification_status fields." }
    - { name: research_gaps,     type: list,      required: false, note: "Areas where the agent could not find independent sourcing — surfaced for partner attention." }
    - { name: agent_notes,       type: string,    required: false, note: "Neutral overall observations: what was easy to verify, what wasn't, what surprised." }

meta.notes:
Per spec constraint: NO LinkedIn scraping. Founder research draws
from the alternative source taxonomy below. Per spec policy: the
agent compiles research material on founders but does NOT score
the team dimension — that remains partner-only (see rubric.yaml).
