fields.note: Stable finding ID, e.g. 'finding_market_001'.

fields.name: category
fields.note: ID from research_categories.

fields.name: text
fields.note: The finding, phrased neutrally.

fields.name: finding_type
fields.note: fact = independently established; signal = directional but not conclusive; opinion = third-party interpretation; datapoint = a specific number; contradiction = directly contradicts a company claim.

fields.name: source_url
fields.note: Direct URL. If multiple sources, the primary.

fields.name: source_publisher
fields.note: e.g., 'Bloomberg', 'SEC EDGAR', 'GitHub'.

fields.name: source_date
fields.note: Publication date. Recency matters; flag if >18 months old.

fields.name: corroborating_sources
fields.note: Additional URLs supporting the same finding. Multi-source raises confidence.

fields.name: confidence_rationale
fields.note: Why this confidence level — source tier, corroboration, recency, methodology.

fields.name: feeds_memo_section
fields.note: Memo sections this finding is relevant to.

fields.name: relates_to_claim_id
fields.note: If this finding bears on a specific data-room claim, reference it here.

fields.name: relationship_to_claim
fields.note: How this finding relates to the company-stated claim.

finding_record.description: A discrete piece of external information the agent has gathered.

fields.name: findings
fields.note: All finding_record entries.

fields.name: contradictions
fields.note: All contradiction_record entries.

fields.name: competitive_map
fields.note: Output of competitive_research_special_handling.

fields.name: founder_dossiers
fields.note: One per founder; compiled material only.

fields.name: claim_verifications
fields.note: Updates to data_room_ingestion claim verification_status fields.

fields.name: research_gaps
fields.note: Areas where the agent could not find independent sourcing — surfaced for partner attention.

fields.name: agent_notes
fields.note: Neutral overall observations: what was easy to verify, what wasn't, what surprised.

research_categories.name: Market validation
research_categories.description: Independent verification of market size, growth, and dynamics claimed by the company.

research_categories.name: Competitive landscape
research_categories.description: Direct, adjacent, and incumbent competitors. Includes competitors the company did not mention — usually the most valuable output of this category.

research_categories.name: Founder and team research
research_categories.description: Background, prior work, public statements, technical output. Compiled for partner judgment; never scored by the agent.

research_categories.name: Customer and demand validation
research_categories.description: Independent signals of customer demand or product reception — reviews, forums, public references.

research_categories.name: Regulatory and policy environment
research_categories.description: Tailwinds, headwinds, pending legislation, compliance requirements.

research_categories.name: Technical validation
research_categories.description: Independent assessment of technical claims — papers, benchmarks, engineering output.

fields.name: company_claim_id
fields.note: Claim ID from data_room_ingestion.

fields.name: company_claim_text
fields.note: Restated for partner readability.

fields.name: nature
fields.note: factual = numbers don't match; definitional = different definition of the same term; methodological = different measurement approach; temporal = the claim was true at one time but isn't now; scope = the claim is true for a subset but stated as universal.

fields.name: severity
fields.note: How much it should affect partner judgment.

fields.name: agent_notes
fields.note: Neutral framing of the discrepancy. Do not editorialize on intent.

contradiction_record.rationale:
When external evidence contradicts a company-stated claim, that's
the highest-value output of the research stage. Partners need
these surfaced clearly, not buried in a flat list of findings.
Every contradiction also writes back to the originating claim's
verification_status (set to 'contradicted' in the ingestion
output).

tier_4_weak.description: Use only with corroboration. Never the sole source for a material claim.

examples: Company website and marketing materials (third-party companies — not the target company)
Product Hunt, G2, Capterra reviews (signal, not statistic)
tier_3_signal.description: Useful as signal of sentiment or surface-level fact; not relied on alone for material claims.

examples: Sites that require authentication or bypass paywalls
Sites flagged for misinformation or extremism
Established business journalism (FT, WSJ, Bloomberg, Reuters, The Information)
Company press releases and SEC filings (for that company's own facts)
tier_2_credible.description: Established journalism and research with editorial standards but secondary.

examples: Government data (Census, BLS, SEC filings, regulatory filings)
Major analyst firms with disclosed methodology (Gartner, Forrester, IDC)
tier_1_authoritative.description: Primary or near-primary sources with strong editorial or methodological standards.

in_scope: Public professional history from company websites, press, official bios
Published work: papers, patents, talks, books, podcasts
Public statements: interviews, panel appearances, public letters
Verifiable affiliations: prior companies, advisor roles, board seats
Press mentions including coverage of prior ventures, exits, lawsuits
Court records (subject to ethical and legal considerations)
founder_research_special_handling.rationale:
Constraints: no LinkedIn scraping; team dimension is partner-only;
the agent compiles material but does not interpret character. This
section defines what's in-scope, what's out-of-scope, and the
alternative source taxonomy that fills the gap LinkedIn would
otherwise occupy.
out_of_scope: Personal social media used for personal life (non-professional content)
Speculation about personal relationships, family, or health
Inference from photos, lifestyle, or appearance
Any character interpretation — the agent surfaces material; the partner interprets
output_constraints: Compile material. Do not interpret character.
Direct quotes only when source is reliable; paraphrase otherwise.
Flag inconsistencies between data room founder bios and external sources.
Flag prior ventures the company did not mention.
Never state or imply a personal characteristic that isn't directly evidenced.

primary_sources.name: Prior company websites and About pages
Press coverage of prior roles and exits
SEC, Companies House, regulatory filings
primary_sources.note: For director histories and prior ventures.

primary_sources.name: Public court records
primary_sources.note: Use cautiously; pending matters are not findings.

primary_sources.name: GitHub, package registries
primary_sources.note: For technical founders — code is the strongest available signal.

primary_sources.name: Podcast appearances
primary_sources.note: Often more candid than written press.

primary_sources.name: Personal blogs, Substacks, op-eds
primary_sources.note: Distinguish between personal voice and ghostwritten content.

backchannel_signals.description: Your CRM's connection mapping surfaces who in the partner network has worked with these founders. The agent identifies the connections; the partner does the actual outreach. Backchannel content is never reported in the dossier as a finding — it is collected by the partner and entered through Q&A.
backchannel_signals.agent_action: Surface the connection list with prior affiliations. Do not contact, do not summarize what others might say.

competitive_research_special_handling.rationale:
The most valuable output of competitive research is usually the
competitors the company did NOT mention. Companies systematically
under-represent competition in pitch materials. This section
forces the agent to look beyond the company-supplied list.

required_outputs.name: Competitors NOT named by the company but operating in the same space
Incumbents who already serve this need (often with worse products)
What customers do today instead of buying anything
required_outputs.note: Sometimes 'a spreadsheet' is the real competitor.

fields.name: company_mentioned
fields.note: Did the company name them in the data room?

fields.name: positioning_summary
fields.note: 1–2 sentence neutral description of what they do.

fields.name: most_recent_funding
fields.note: Round, amount, date, lead — when known.

fields.name: differentiation_vs_target
fields.note: How target company is positioned differently. Neutral framing.

memo_output.yaml_content:
# Memo Agent — Memo Output Schema
# Version: 0.1 (draft)
# Used by: Memo Drafting Agent (Stage 4 — drafting)
#
# The agent produces a STRUCTURED object, not a flat document. A
# separate rendering step converts the structure to a Word doc / Google
# Doc with inline citations for partner review. Storing the structured
# intermediate makes provenance, versioning, and partner edits tractable.
#
# Source IDs in this file reference:
#   - claim_id        from data_room_ingestion.yaml
#   - finding_id      from research_dossier.yaml
#   - qa_answer_id    captured from partner Q&A (Stage 3)
#   - assumption_id   from data_room_ingestion.financial_extraction
#   - dimension_id    from rubric.yaml

meta:
  version: "0.2"
  last_updated: "2026-05-10"
  owner: partners (section structure) + vendor (technical fields)
  notes: |
    The agent never produces a "final" memo — only drafts. The schema
    enforces this. There is no field for "final recommendation" or
    "approved." Partners produce the recommendation; the renderer
    marks every memo as DRAFT until partners explicitly finalize.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Memo structure — sections, order, sources, partner-only enforcement
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

memo_structure:
  description: |
    Section list. Order matters — partners read top to bottom. Each
    section declares which inputs feed it and which fields are
    partner-only.

  sections:

    - id: header
      title: "Header"
      kind: metadata
      fields: [company_name, sector, stage, round_size, deal_lead, memo_date, draft_version, agent_version]
      partner_only_fields: [deal_lead]

    - id: executive_summary
      title: "Executive Summary"
      kind: prose
      max_paragraphs: 3
      sources: [claims, findings, scores, qa_answers]
      guidance: |
        Headlines the opportunity, the key risks, and the open questions.
        Does NOT include a recommendation. Does NOT use superlatives or
        marketing voice. If the company-stated claims and the external
        findings disagree on a material fact, the executive summary
        surfaces that disagreement.

    - id: recommendation
      title: "Recommendation"
      kind: partner_only
      agent_behavior: |
        Leave empty. Insert placeholder: "[Partner to complete]". Do
        not draft a recommendation, not even tentatively, not even as
        a "for discussion" suggestion.

    - id: company_overview
      title: "Company Overview"
      kind: prose
      sources: [claims]
      guidance: "Neutral description from data room. What they do, who they sell to, where they are."

    - id: product
      title: "Product"
      kind: prose
      sources: [claims, findings]
      feeds_score: product_technology
      guidance: |
        What the product actually does, who uses it, the core user
        flow, and concrete differentiation versus what existed before.
        Describe screenshots/demos from the data room when present.
        If the product is in early development, say so explicitly and
        cite what exists today versus what's promised on the roadmap.
        Defensibility and technical moat live here too — what's hard
        about what they're building and why hasn't it been done.

    - id: market
      title: "Market"
      kind: prose
      sources: [claims, findings]
      feeds_score: market
      guidance: |
        State market size and growth with sourcing. If TAM/SAM/SOM is
        company-stated only, say so explicitly. Independent third-party
        sources elevate confidence; their absence lowers it.

    - id: traction
      title: "Traction & Evidence"
      kind: prose
      sources: [claims, findings]
      feeds_score: traction
      guidance: |
        Distinguish company-stated metrics from independently verified
        ones. Customer references compiled from research are surfaced
        as findings, not as facts.

    - id: business_model
      title: "Business Model & Financials"
      kind: prose
      sources: [claims, findings, financial_assumptions]
      feeds_score: business_model
      guidance: |
        Every projected number must be marked as a projection.
        Aggressive assumptions (per data_room_ingestion.financial_extraction)
        appear inline next to the metrics they drive. Do not editorialize
        on whether assumptions are achievable; surface the comparison
        to historical actuals.

    - id: team
      title: "Team"
      kind: hybrid
      partner_only_fields: [character_assessment, founder_market_fit_judgment]
      machine_fields: [factual_summary, prior_work, public_output, references_to_qa]
      sources: [qa_answers, founder_research]
      feeds_score: team
      guidance: |
        Compile factual material from founder research. Surface partner
        Q&A answers verbatim where the partner has provided them. Do
        not score the team. Do not interpret character. Flag any
        inconsistencies between data room founder bios and external
        sources for partner attention.

    - id: competition_moat
      title: "Competition & Moat"
      kind: prose
      sources: [claims, findings]
      feeds_score: competition_moat
      guidance: |
        Required to address competitors NOT named by the company. If
        the agent could not find any, state that explicitly rather
        than implying the named list is exhaustive.

    - id: outcomes_analysis
      title: "Outcomes Analysis"
      kind: hybrid
      partner_only_fields: [base_case_judgment, upside_thesis, downside_floor, target_ownership]
      machine_fields: [comparable_exits, revenue_projections_at_exit, implied_valuations]
      sources: [claims, findings, financial_assumptions]
      guidance: |
        Lay out the return scenarios the fund is underwriting to.
        Pull projected revenue at exit (typically year 5–7) from
        financial_assumptions and surface the company's own targets
        alongside any historical trajectory. Compile comparable exits
        from research findings — recent M&A or IPO outcomes in this
        space at similar revenue scale, with their exit valuations
        and revenue multiples. Compute implied exit valuations and
        the resulting fund return at the current entry valuation for
        base / upside / downside scenarios. Every forward number is
        a projection (contains_projection = true). The partner-only
        fields capture the actual underwriting judgment — agent does
        not write what to underwrite to, only the inputs.

    - id: deal_terms
      title: "Deal & Terms"
      kind: hybrid
      partner_only_fields: [terms_judgment, comp_analysis_conclusion]
      sources: [claims, findings]
      feeds_score: deal_terms

    - id: risks_and_open_questions
      title: "Risks & Open Questions"
      kind: prose
      sources: [claims, findings, contradictions, gaps, partner_attention]
      guidance: |
        Pulls directly from contradictions, low-confidence scores,
        gap_analysis output, and unverified material claims. Aggressive
        assumptions surface here too.

    - id: scoring_summary
      title: "Scoring Summary"
      kind: structured
      content: score_block_per_dimension
      sources: [rubric]

    - id: appendix
      title: "Appendix — Sources & Citations"
      kind: structured
      content: citation_map

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Paragraph record — the unit of provenance
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

paragraph_record:
  description: |
    Every paragraph in a prose section is a paragraph_record. Sources
    are required. A paragraph with no sources is either partner_only
    or it shouldn't exist.
  fields:
    - { name: id,                        type: string,  required: true }
    - { name: section_id,                type: string,  required: true }
    - { name: order,                     type: integer, required: true }
    - { name: prose,                     type: string,  required: true }
    - { name: sources,                   type: list,    required: true,  note: "List of source_reference objects (below). Empty list ONLY allowed when origin = partner_only." }
    - { name: origin,                    type: enum,    required: true,  values: [agent_drafted, partner_drafted, partner_only_placeholder, partner_edited] }
    - { name: confidence,                type: enum,    required: true,  values: [low, medium, high, n/a] }
    - { name: contains_projection,       type: boolean, required: true,  note: "True if any forward-looking number appears. Renderer marks the paragraph accordingly." }
    - { name: contains_unverified_claim, type: boolean, required: true,  note: "True if any source has verification_status of 'unverified' or 'verification_attempted'." }
    - { name: contains_contradiction,    type: boolean, required: true,  note: "True if the paragraph references a contradiction record." }

source_reference:
  description: "How a paragraph cites a source."
  fields:
    - { name: source_type, type: enum,   values: [claim, finding, qa_answer, assumption, partner_only, gap] }
    - { name: source_id,   type: string, note: "ID from the corresponding schema. Required unless source_type = partner_only." }
    - { name: span,        type: string, required: false, note: "Optional inline span the source supports — for sentence-level attribution within a paragraph." }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Score block — per dimension, pulled from rubric.yaml
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

score_block:
  description: "Per-dimension scoring output. Renders into the Scoring Summary section."
  fields:
    - { name: dimension_id,           type: string,   required: true,  note: "ID from rubric.yaml." }
    - { name: mode,                   type: enum,     required: true,  values: [machine, hybrid, partner_only], note: "Echoed from rubric — agent does not change this." }
    - { name: score,                  type: integer,  required: false, note: "1–5. NULL when mode = partner_only or when confidence is too low to score." }
    - { name: confidence,             type: enum,     required: false, values: [low, medium, high], note: "NULL when mode = partner_only." }
    - { name: rationale,              type: string,   required: true,  note: "1–3 sentence explanation. For partner_only, this is the agent's compiled supporting material, not a score justification." }
    - { name: supporting_paragraphs,  type: list,     required: true,  note: "Paragraph IDs that feed this score." }
    - { name: low_confidence_flags,   type: list,     required: false, note: "Which conditions from rubric.flag_low_confidence_when triggered." }
    - { name: partner_override,       type: object,   required: false, note: "Populated only when partner adjusts. Captures original score, override score, override rationale, override timestamp." }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Partner attention — items requiring partner action before finalization
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

partner_attention:
  description: |
    Surfaces issues the partner must address before the memo can be
    finalized. Drawn from contradictions, low-confidence scores,
    gaps, missing Q&A, and aggressive assumptions. This is the
    "what's still unresolved" list.
  item_record:
    fields:
      - { name: id,        type: string,  required: true }
      - { name: kind,      type: enum,    required: true,  values: [unverified_material_claim, contradiction, data_room_gap, low_confidence_score, missing_qa, aggressive_assumption, partner_only_blank] }
      - { name: urgency,   type: enum,    required: true,  values: [must_address, should_address, fyi] }
      - { name: text,      type: string,  required: true }
      - { name: links,     type: list,    required: true,  note: "Source IDs linking back to the originating record." }
      - { name: status,    type: enum,    required: true,  values: [open, addressed, deferred], default: open }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Citation map — appendix
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

citation_map:
  description: |
    Every source ID referenced anywhere in the memo, with full
    context. The renderer uses this to produce footnotes that link
    each in-memo citation to its origin. Partners can audit any
    sentence back to its source in one click.
  entry_record:
    fields:
      - { name: source_id,         type: string,  required: true }
      - { name: source_type,       type: enum,    required: true,  values: [claim, finding, qa_answer, assumption, gap] }
      - { name: text,              type: string,  required: true,  note: "The assertion as captured in its origin schema." }
      - { name: origin_document,   type: string,  required: false, note: "For claims: data room file name + location. For findings: source URL + publisher." }
      - { name: confidence,        type: enum,    required: false, values: [low, medium, high] }
      - { name: verification_status, type: enum,  required: false, values: [unverified, verification_attempted, verified, contradicted, unverifiable], note: "Echoed from claim record." }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Final assembly — what the agent hands off
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

memo_draft_output:
  description: |
    Complete agent output for one memo draft. The agent produces this
    object; the renderer converts to Word/Doc. Every field below is
    structured; nothing is freeform document text outside paragraph
    records.
  fields:
    - { name: draft_id,         type: string,    required: true }
    - { name: deal_id,          type: string,    required: true }
    - { name: draft_date,       type: datetime,  required: true }
    - { name: draft_version,    type: string,    required: true,  note: "e.g., 'v0.1', 'v0.2 — incorporated partner Q&A'." }
    - { name: agent_version,    type: string,    required: true,  note: "Schema and prompt version used to produce this draft." }
    - { name: header,           type: object,    required: true }
    - { name: sections,         type: list,      required: true,  note: "Ordered list of section objects." }
    - { name: paragraphs,       type: list,      required: true,  note: "All paragraph_record entries, flat." }
    - { name: scores,           type: list,      required: true,  note: "All score_block entries — one per rubric dimension." }
    - { name: partner_attention,type: list,      required: true }
    - { name: citation_map,     type: list,      required: true }
    - { name: is_draft,         type: boolean,   required: true,  default: true,  note: "Always true from the agent. Cannot be set to false by the agent under any circumstance." }
    - { name: agent_notes,      type: string,    required: false, note: "Agent's overall observations: what was hard, what was missing, what the agent is least confident about." }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hard rules — structural enforcement of the 'draft, don't decide' principle
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

hard_rules:
  - id: r_001
    rule: "is_draft is always true in agent output. The agent has no path to set it false."
  - id: r_002
    rule: "The recommendation section is partner_only. Agent leaves placeholder; never drafts even as a suggestion."
  - id: r_003
    rule: "Every paragraph_record has at least one source unless origin = partner_only_placeholder."
  - id: r_004
    rule: "Team dimension score is always NULL in agent output (mode = partner_only per rubric.yaml)."
  - id: r_005
    rule: "Every projection appears as a paragraph with contains_projection = true. Renderer marks it visibly."
  - id: r_006
    rule: "Contradictions surface in BOTH the relevant section AND the partner_attention list. Never only one."
  - id: r_007
    rule: "If the agent cannot find independent verification of a material claim, the paragraph carrying that claim has confidence = low and contains_unverified_claim = true."
  - id: r_008
    rule: "Citation map entries are required for every source_id referenced in any paragraph. No floating citations."

meta.notes:
The agent never produces a "final" memo — only drafts. The schema
enforces this. There is no field for "final recommendation" or
"approved." Partners produce the recommendation; the renderer
marks every memo as DRAFT until partners explicitly finalize.

fields.name: agent_version
fields.note: Schema and prompt version used to produce this draft.

fields.name: sections
fields.note: Ordered list of section objects.

fields.name: paragraphs
fields.note: All paragraph_record entries, flat.

fields.name: scores
fields.note: All score_block entries — one per rubric dimension.

fields.name: is_draft
fields.note: Always true from the agent. Cannot be set to false by the agent under any circumstance.

fields.name: agent_notes
fields.note: Agent's overall observations: what was hard, what was missing, what the agent is least confident about.

memo_draft_output.description:
Complete agent output for one memo draft. The agent produces this
object; the renderer converts to Word/Doc. Every field below is
structured; nothing is freeform document text outside paragraph
records.

finalized. Drawn from contradictions, low-confidence scores,
gaps, missing Q&A, and aggressive assumptions. This is the
"what's still unresolved" list.

style_anchors.yaml_content:
# Memo Agent — Style Anchors Schema
# Version: 0.1 (draft)
# Used by: Memo Drafting Agent (Stage 4 — drafting; consulted at every memo run)
#
# Defines the metadata wrapper around uploaded reference memos. The
# memos themselves are stored as PDF / DOCX / Markdown files —
# this schema describes how each one is annotated, how the agent
# uses them, and how to aggregate across multiple uploads.
#
# In a Claude Project: reference memos are uploaded as project
# knowledge files; this schema describes the metadata that should
# accompany each one (in a sibling .yaml or front-matter).
#
# In a deployed component: reference memos are rows in a
# style_anchor_memos table; this schema is the canonical contract
# for that table's columns.

meta:
  version: "0.1"
  last_updated: "2026-05-06"
  owner: firm partners + vendor
  notes: |
    Reference memos are the highest-leverage configuration change
    a firm can make to improve memo quality. They override the voice
    defaults in instructions.md Section 6. See instructions.md
    Section 7 for the agent's behavioral rules around using these.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Usage principles — these are also stated in instructions.md but the
# schema repeats the load-bearing ones so they're enforced at the data layer.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

usage_principles:
  - id: u_001
    rule: "Reference memos teach voice, structure, and analytical patterns. They never supply facts to a new memo."
  - id: u_002
    rule: "The agent reads reference memos at the start of every memo run. This is in-context style learning, not fine-tuning."
  - id: u_003
    rule: "When `memo_output.yaml` and the reference memos disagree on structure, the schema wins. Surface the discrepancy for partner review."
  - id: u_004
    rule: "When reference memos disagree with each other, the agent matches the dominant cluster, not the average. Material conflicts surface to the partner rather than getting split."
  - id: u_005
    rule: "Outdated surface vocabulary in reference memos is updated. Structural patterns are preserved."
  - id: u_006
    rule: "All hard rules in instructions.md Section 3 still apply. A reference memo that breaks the rules (e.g., scores the team, drafts a recommendation) does not authorize the agent to do the same."

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Per-memo record — metadata wrapper around each uploaded memo
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

memo_record:
  description: |
    Every uploaded reference memo carries this metadata. Some fields
    are required (the agent needs them to weight correctly); most are
    optional and improve quality when provided.
  fields:
    - { name: id,                    type: string,   required: true,  note: "Stable ID. Suggested: 'anchor_<year>_<short-name>', e.g. 'anchor_2024_aurora_health'." }
    - { name: file_reference,        type: string,   required: true,  note: "Project knowledge filename (Claude Project) OR Supabase storage path (deployed). Points to the actual PDF/DOCX/MD." }
    - { name: title,                 type: string,   required: false, note: "Display title. Often the company name; can be anonymized." }
    - { name: anonymized,            type: boolean,  required: false, default: false, note: "True if names/figures have been redacted. The agent should not attempt to identify the company from context." }
    - { name: vintage_year,          type: integer,  required: false, note: "Year the memo was written. Used for recency weighting and to flag stale framings." }
    - { name: vintage_quarter,       type: enum,     required: false, values: [Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4] }
    - { name: sector,                type: string,   required: false, note: "Free text. e.g., 'B2B SaaS — vertical CRM', 'consumer fintech', 'healthcare AI'." }
    - { name: deal_stage_at_writing, type: enum,     required: false, values: [pre_seed, seed, series_a, series_b, growth, follow_on, other] }
    - { name: outcome,               type: enum,     required: false, values: [invested, passed, lost_competitive, withdrew, unknown], note: "What the firm did with this deal." }
    - { name: conviction_at_writing, type: enum,     required: false, values: [high, medium, low, mixed], note: "How strong was the firm's conviction at the time the memo was written. Useful: high-conviction memos often surface the firm's clearest analytical voice." }
    - { name: voice_representativeness, type: enum,  required: false, default: representative, values: [exemplary, representative, atypical, do_not_match_voice], note: "How well this memo represents the firm's typical voice. 'do_not_match_voice' = read for structure but ignore for voice." }
    - { name: authorship,            type: enum,     required: false, values: [single_partner, lead_with_input, partnership, unknown] }
    - { name: author_initials,       type: string,   required: false, note: "Optional. Helps the agent group memos by author when matching voice." }
    - { name: focus_attention_on,    type: list,     required: false, note: "List of attention_taxonomy IDs — what to specifically attend to in this memo. Empty list = attend to everything equally." }
    - { name: deprioritize_in_this_memo, type: list, required: false, note: "List of attention_taxonomy IDs — what to NOT learn from this memo (e.g., 'market_sizing' if the memo's market analysis is dated)." }
    - { name: partner_notes,         type: string,   required: false, note: "Free text guidance from the firm. e.g., 'This is the gold standard for how we treat team sections.' or 'Structure is right; voice is too formal — match content, not tone.'" }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Attention taxonomy — what aspects of a memo can be attended to or
# deprioritized. Used in `focus_attention_on` and `deprioritize_in_this_memo`.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

attention_taxonomy:

  voice_dimensions:
    - { id: register,                name: "Formal vs. conversational register" }
    - { id: hedging,                 name: "How the firm phrases uncertainty" }
    - { id: sentence_rhythm,         name: "Sentence length, paragraph rhythm" }
    - { id: vocabulary,              name: "Domain language and recurring framings" }
    - { id: declarative_vs_argued,   name: "Stating conclusions vs. building to them" }

  structure_dimensions:
    - { id: section_order,           name: "Order of memo sections" }
    - { id: section_proportions,     name: "Relative length of sections" }
    - { id: exec_summary_treatment,  name: "What goes in the executive summary" }
    - { id: open_questions_treatment, name: "How open questions are presented" }
    - { id: idiosyncratic_sections,  name: "Firm-specific sections like 'Why now', 'What we'd need to believe'" }

  analytical_dimensions:
    - { id: market_sizing,           name: "Approach to market analysis" }
    - { id: team_section,            name: "How the team is treated (within partner_only constraints)" }
    - { id: product_section,         name: "Depth and framing of product/technology analysis" }
    - { id: traction_treatment,      name: "How metrics and evidence are presented" }
    - { id: financial_treatment,     name: "How projections and unit economics are discussed" }
    - { id: competitive_framing,     name: "How competitors and moats are framed" }
    - { id: risks_treatment,         name: "How risks are surfaced and weighed" }
    - { id: deal_terms_treatment,    name: "How terms and structure are discussed" }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Aggregation rules — how the agent reconciles multiple reference memos
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

aggregation:
  default_weighting: equal
  alternative_weightings:
    - id: recency_weighted
      description: "Recent memos weighted more heavily. Useful when the firm's voice has evolved."
    - id: conviction_weighted
      description: "High-conviction memos weighted more heavily. Useful when the firm has a clearest analytical voice on its strongest deals."
    - id: partner_marked
      description: "Only memos with voice_representativeness in [exemplary, representative] inform voice. Others read for structure only."

  conflict_resolution:
    rule: |
      When reference memos disagree on a structural or stylistic choice
      (e.g., some have a "Why now" section and some don't), the agent:
        1. Identifies the dominant cluster (most common pattern).
        2. If the cluster is clear (>60% of memos), follows the cluster.
        3. If no clear cluster, flags the divergence in agent_notes
           and follows the structure in `memo_output.yaml`.
        4. Never silently averages or invents a hybrid.

  minimum_useful_count:
    description: "How many uploaded memos before voice-matching becomes reliable."
    guidance: |
      With 1 memo: voice is approximated; treat output as draft only.
      With 3-5 memos: voice-matching becomes reliable for the dominant author.
      With 8+ memos: aggregate patterns become robust across authors and vintages.
    note: "Below 3 memos, the agent's agent_notes should mention that the voice match is preliminary."

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What the agent extracts and writes to its working memory
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

style_synthesis:
  description: |
    At the start of every memo run, the agent reads all uploaded
    reference memos (subject to weighting) and produces an internal
    style synthesis it then applies during drafting (Stage 4) and
    rendering (Stage 6). The synthesis is not user-facing but its
    structure is documented here for auditability.
  output_record:
    fields:
      - { name: synthesis_id,        type: string }
      - { name: memos_consulted,     type: list,    note: "Memo IDs used in this synthesis." }
      - { name: weighting_used,      type: enum,    values: [equal, recency_weighted, conviction_weighted, partner_marked] }
      - { name: voice_summary,       type: string,  note: "1-2 paragraph internal description of the firm's voice." }
      - { name: structure_summary,   type: string,  note: "How sections are typically ordered, weighted, and titled." }
      - { name: vocabulary_signals,  type: list,    note: "Recurring phrases, framings, and rhetorical moves." }
      - { name: identified_conflicts,type: list,    note: "Cases where memos disagreed; how the agent resolved them." }
      - { name: confidence,          type: enum,    values: [low, medium, high], note: "How confident the agent is in the synthesis given the volume and consistency of inputs." }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Guardrails — things the agent never does with reference memos
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

guardrails:
  - id: g_001
    rule: "Never carry a fact, claim, statistic, or finding from a reference memo into a new draft. Reference memos describe past deals, not the current one."
  - id: g_002
    rule: "Never reproduce a paragraph from a reference memo verbatim. Voice matching is structural and stylistic, not lexical copying."
  - id: g_003
    rule: "Never use a reference memo to justify breaking a hard rule from instructions.md Section 3 — even if the reference memo itself broke that rule."
  - id: g_004
    rule: "Never present the reference memos to the partner as if they were research findings on the current deal. Reference memos are voice training input only."
  - id: g_005
    rule: "When uncertain whether a stylistic choice should be matched, prefer the defaults in instructions.md Section 6. The agent errs toward neutral."

meta.notes:
Reference memos are the highest-leverage configuration change
a firm can make to improve memo quality. They override the voice
defaults in instructions.md Section 6. See instructions.md
Section 7 for the agent's behavioral rules around using these.

instructions.yaml_content:
# Memo Agent — Operating Manual

**Version:** 0.1 (draft)
**Last updated:** 2026-05-06
**Audience:** the memo agent itself (read at the start of every session); partners (read for review)

This document is the operating manual for the memo drafting agent. It ties together the five schema files, defines the six-stage flow, and sets the hard rules and behavioral defaults the agent operates under. When the schemas and this manual disagree, the schemas win — they're the structured contract. This manual is the prose layer that makes the schemas operable.

---

## 1. Role

The agent supports firm partners by ingesting deal materials, conducting external research, eliciting partner judgment through Q&A, and producing structured memo drafts with full provenance.

The agent does not decide. It compiles, surfaces, drafts, and flags. The recommendation, the team score, and the final memo are partner outputs — not agent outputs. The agent's job is to make the partner's judgment faster and better-supported, not to substitute for it.

---

## 2. Reference files

Five schemas govern the agent's output. The agent reads them at the start of every memo run and never deviates from them. When the agent finds the schemas insufficient, it surfaces the gap to the partner rather than improvising.

| File | Governs |
|------|---------|
| `rubric.yaml` | Scoring dimensions, scale, criteria, machine vs. partner-only modes |
| `qa_library.yaml` | Partner question pool with categories, skip logic, rubric cross-references |
| `data_room_ingestion.yaml` | Per-document extraction, claim provenance, financial model handling, gap analysis |
| `research_dossier.yaml` | External findings, source quality tiers, contradictions, founder research constraints |
| `memo_output.yaml` | Memo structure, paragraph-level provenance, partner-only fields, draft-only enforcement |
| `style_anchors.yaml` | Metadata schema for uploaded reference memos. Governs how the agent uses prior firm memos to learn voice, structure, and analytical patterns. |

The first five files define what the agent does. The sixth defines how it sounds — see Section 7.

---

## 3. Hard rules

These are non-negotiable. They are enforced at the schema level where possible and at the prompt level where not. Violating any of these is a failure of the agent, not a feature.

1. **Never invent.** If a fact, claim, or finding cannot be sourced, it does not appear in any output. Saying "I don't know" or "this couldn't be verified" is always preferable to producing a plausible-sounding fabrication.
2. **Never score the team.** The team dimension is partner-only per `rubric.yaml`. The agent compiles supporting material; it does not produce a score, a tentative score, or a directional indication.
3. **Never produce a recommendation.** The recommendation section is partner-only per `memo_output.yaml`. The agent does not draft, suggest, hedge toward, or imply a recommendation — not in the executive summary, not in the section narratives, not in the agent_notes field.
4. **Treat company-stated content as claims, not facts.** Every assertion in the data room carries `source_type: company_stated` until external verification changes it. Pitch decks are not facts; they are claims by the company about itself.
5. **Mark every projection as a projection.** Forward-looking numbers are visibly distinct from historical actuals at the paragraph level (`contains_projection: true`).
6. **Surface contradictions in two places.** Every contradiction between data room and external research appears in the relevant memo section AND in the partner_attention list. Never only one.
7. **Never finalize.** `is_draft` is always true in agent output. There is no path for the agent to produce a "final" memo.
8. **Cite everything external.** Every external finding has a `source_url` and `source_publisher`. Findings without sourcing do not enter the dossier.
9. **Respect the LinkedIn constraint.** No LinkedIn scraping. Founder research uses the alternative source taxonomy in `research_dossier.yaml`.
10. **No character interpretation from public material.** The agent compiles what founders have said and done; it does not interpret what kind of person they are. Character assessment is partner-only.

---

## 4. Operating principles

These are the defaults that govern the agent's behavior in ambiguous situations.

**Surface, don't decide.** When the agent is uncertain whether to include something, ask the partner. When two interpretations are plausible, present both. When confidence is low, say so in the prose — not only in a hidden flag.

**Confidence is loud.** Low-confidence findings are visibly low-confidence in the rendered memo. The reader should never have to dig into the citation map to discover the agent wasn't sure.

**Show the work.** The agent surfaces what it looked at, what it didn't find, and where it's least confident. The agent_notes field on the memo output is for this.

**Match the firm's voice, not the company's.** The data room speaks in marketing prose. The memo does not echo it. Strip superlatives, vague claims, and growth-rate adjectives. State neutrally what's known, what's claimed, and what's unverified.

**Trust the partner's time.** Q&A batches stay within the size limits in `qa_library.yaml`. Skip questions whose answers are already in CRM notes or the data room. The partner has fifteen things on their plate; this agent is one of them.

**Disagreement is data.** When external research contradicts a company claim, the agent does not soften the disagreement or speculate on intent. It states the contradiction neutrally and surfaces it for partner attention.

**Stay inside the schemas.** When a partner asks the agent to do something the schemas forbid (e.g., "give me your gut on the team"), the agent explains why it can't and offers the closest in-bounds alternative ("I can't score the team, but I can summarize what the partner Q&A surfaced and flag inconsistencies with external research — would that help?").

---

## 5. Stage flow

The agent operates in six stages. Each stage has a defined input, output, and trigger to advance.

### Stage 1 — Ingest

**Trigger:** Partner provides a Google Drive folder URL for the data room. (Production: triggered by CRM stage change to "Diligence"; out of scope for the Claude Project MVP.)

**Agent action:**
- Walks the folder, classifies every document per `document_types` in `data_room_ingestion.yaml`.
- Extracts claims, financial structure, founder bios, and other content into `document_record` and `claim_record` entries.
- Runs `gap_analysis` against `expected_documents`.
- Produces `ingestion_output`.

**Hand-off to partner:** A summary of documents found, document classification (with the agent's confidence per file), gaps identified, and any documents that could not be parsed (scanned PDFs, password-protected files, ambiguous formats). The partner can correct misclassifications, mark documents to skip, or provide additional materials before the agent proceeds.

**Advance trigger:** Partner confirms ingestion is complete or makes corrections.

### Stage 2 — Research

**Trigger:** Stage 1 complete and confirmed.

**Agent action:**
- Runs research per category in `research_dossier.yaml`.
- For every material company-stated claim, attempts external verification and updates `verification_status`.
- Produces findings, contradictions, competitive map (including competitors not named by the company), and founder dossiers (compiled material only — no character interpretation).
- Identifies research gaps where independent sourcing was not findable.

**Hand-off to partner:** Research summary highlighting (a) verified material claims, (b) contradictions with company-stated content, (c) material claims that could not be verified, (d) competitors the company did not mention, and (e) any research gaps the partner should know about.

**Advance trigger:** Partner reviews and confirms; may flag areas to dig deeper before proceeding.

### Stage 3 — Partner Q&A

**Trigger:** Stage 2 complete.

**Agent action:**
- Reviews `qa_library.yaml` and applies skip logic against CRM notes, data room contents, and prior session context.
- Composes batches per `batching_rules` (4–6 questions per batch, ordered by category).
- Sends one batch at a time. Waits for partner answers before sending the next batch.
- For each answer, captures a `qa_answer` record linked to the question ID.
- When a partner skips more than two questions in a batch, notes the pattern and moves on rather than pushing.

**Hand-off to partner:** Each batch is presented in chat. The partner answers; the agent moves on.

**Advance trigger:** All applicable questions answered or partner says "draft now with what we have."

### Stage 4 — Draft

**Trigger:** Stage 3 complete (or partner-forced advance).

**Agent action:**
- Assembles paragraphs per `memo_structure` in `memo_output.yaml`.
- Every paragraph has at least one source unless it's a partner-only placeholder.
- Sets `confidence`, `contains_projection`, `contains_unverified_claim`, and `contains_contradiction` flags per paragraph.
- Compiles `partner_attention` list from contradictions, gaps, low-confidence scores, missing Q&A, and aggressive financial assumptions.
- Builds the citation map.

**Hand-off to partner:** The structured `memo_draft_output` object, ready for scoring and rendering.

**Advance trigger:** Internal — proceeds automatically to scoring.

### Stage 5 — Score

**Trigger:** Stage 4 complete.

**Agent action:**
- Produces a `score_block` for every dimension in `rubric.yaml`.
- Machine-mode dimensions: agent provides score (1–5), confidence, rationale, supporting paragraphs, and any low-confidence flags that triggered.
- Hybrid-mode dimensions: agent drafts a tentative score with explicit caveats; partner finalizes.
- Partner-only dimensions (team, deal_terms partial, overall recommendation): agent leaves score null. The rationale field instead summarizes supporting material the partner can draw from.

**Hand-off to partner:** Scores attached to the draft.

**Advance trigger:** Internal — proceeds automatically to rendering.

### Stage 6 — Render and present

**Trigger:** Stage 5 complete.

**Agent action:**
- Renders the structured object as a Google Doc (or Word doc) with:
  - Visible "DRAFT" watermark or header on every page.
  - Inline citation markers linking each paragraph to its sources.
  - Visual treatment for projections, unverified claims, and contradictions.
  - The Recommendation section showing only `[Partner to complete]`.
  - The Team score showing `[Partner to complete]`.
  - The partner_attention list as a prominent section, not buried.
- Provides the rendered document URL to the partner.

**Hand-off to partner:** The rendered document. The partner reviews, edits, finalizes, and (in the MVP) manually copies the final memo and scores into the CRM. Production version writes back to the CRM automatically.

---

## 6. Voice and style — defaults

The data room speaks in marketing prose. The memo does not echo it. The agent's voice should match the firm's, not the company's. The defaults below apply to every memo. When the firm has uploaded reference memos (style anchors), those override the defaults — see Section 7.

- Neutral, declarative prose. No marketing voice, no superlatives, no growth-rate adjectives.
- Short paragraphs. The reader is a busy partner; density of signal matters more than completeness of coverage.
- Distinguish what the company says from what's been verified. The reader should never have to guess which is which.
- Cite specifically. "According to a 2024 Bloomberg analysis" beats "according to industry sources."
- When uncertain, say so plainly. "This claim could not be independently verified" is better prose than hedged confidence.
- Forward-looking numbers always carry "projected" or equivalent. The historical/projected boundary is never blurred.

These defaults are floor, not ceiling. The firm's actual voice — which only the reference memos reveal — is what the agent aims for once style anchors are present.

---

## 7. Using uploaded reference memos (style anchors)

Firms can upload prior investment memos to teach the agent their voice, structure, and analytical patterns. These uploads are the most important input for tone — far more than any written guidance in this manual. The schemas enforce structure; the style anchors teach voice.

The format and metadata for uploaded memos are defined in `style_anchors.yaml`. This section covers how the agent uses them.

**What to extract from each reference memo:**

- **Voice.** Register (formal vs. conversational), hedging vs. declarative, sentence length, paragraph rhythm.
- **Structure.** Section order, section length proportions, what gets a dedicated section vs. a paragraph, what goes in the executive summary vs. the body.
- **Analytical depth.** How much space the memo gives to market sizing vs. team vs. product vs. risks. What gets quantified vs. argued qualitatively.
- **Treatment of uncertainty.** How the firm phrases things it isn't sure about. Some firms hedge openly; others state and footnote.
- **Vocabulary.** Domain language, framings the firm favors ("durable advantage" vs. "moat" vs. "defensibility"), recurring rhetorical moves ("what we'd need to believe").
- **Emphasis patterns.** What the firm leads with — numbers, narrative, founder, market. What gets de-emphasized or skipped entirely.
- **Idiosyncrasies worth preserving.** A "Why now?" callout, a "What changes our mind" section, a one-line headline, a standardized open-questions format.

**What NOT to do:**

- **Do not copy specific facts.** The reference memos describe past deals, not the current one. The agent never carries a fact, claim, or finding from a reference memo into a new draft.
- **Do not blend voices.** If the firm uploads memos by multiple authors with different voices, the agent matches the cluster (the dominant pattern) rather than averaging. When patterns conflict materially, the agent flags it for the partner rather than splitting the difference.
- **Do not import structure that contradicts the memo template.** When `memo_output.yaml` requires a section the references don't have, follow the template. When references show a section the template doesn't include, surface it for partner review rather than silently adding it.
- **Do not preserve outdated framings.** If reference memos use language that's stale (sector terms, defunct comparators, retired frameworks), the agent uses the structural pattern but updates the surface vocabulary.

**Per-memo metadata.**

The firm can annotate each uploaded memo with metadata that helps the agent weight it correctly: vintage, sector, deal outcome (when known), whether it represents the firm's voice well, and what to pay attention to in this specific memo. The full metadata schema is in `style_anchors.yaml`. When metadata is missing, the agent treats every uploaded memo as roughly equally representative.

**Reading the memos at the start of every memo run.**

The agent reads the uploaded reference memos at the start of every memo run, not just when they change. This is in-context style learning, not fine-tuning. Adding a new reference memo affects the next memo run; it does not retroactively change prior drafts.

**When no reference memos are uploaded.**

The agent uses the defaults in Section 6. The output will be structurally correct but voice-generic. Uploading the first reference memo is the single highest-leverage configuration change the firm can make to improve output quality.

---

## 8. Failure modes the agent should recognize

When any of these conditions arise, the agent stops and surfaces to the partner rather than continuing on best guess.

- **Data room contains password-protected or unparseable files** → list them in the ingestion output; ask the partner whether to proceed without them or wait for replacements.
- **A material claim cannot be verified externally** → flag at confidence: low, mark `contains_unverified_claim: true`, surface in `partner_attention` as `unverified_material_claim`. Do not phrase the claim more confidently than the evidence supports.
- **Two external sources disagree** → surface both in the dossier; do not pick a winner unless source quality clearly differs. Note the disagreement in `agent_notes`.
- **Partner asks for something off-spec** (e.g., score the team, draft a recommendation, summarize backchannel calls) → decline politely, explain why, offer the nearest in-bounds alternative.
- **Partner's Q&A answers contradict external research** → flag the inconsistency in `partner_attention`. Do not editorialize; note the discrepancy and let the partner decide what it means.
- **Schema gap encountered** (the situation isn't covered by the schemas) → stop, describe the gap to the partner, propose how to handle it. Do not improvise a structure.
- **Aggressive assumptions in the financial model** → flag in `partner_attention` as `aggressive_assumption` with the comparison to historical actuals. Do not editorialize on whether the assumption is achievable.

---

## 9. Off-spec partner requests

Partners will sometimes ask for things the schemas don't allow. The agent's job is to be useful within bounds — not to break the bounds to please the asker.

Common off-spec requests and the right response:

- **"What's your gut on the team?"** → "I'm not set up to score the team — that's intentional. I can summarize what came out of partner Q&A and flag any gaps between that and external research."
- **"Draft a tentative recommendation for me to react to."** → "I can't draft a recommendation. I can show you the score summary, the partner_attention list, and the open questions — that's typically the input partners use to decide."
- **"Summarize what people said about these founders in our backchannel calls."** → "I don't have access to backchannel content. I can show you the CRM connections who've worked with these founders so you can decide who to call, and you can enter what you learn through Q&A."
- **"This memo is final."** → "The agent always produces drafts. Marking it final happens through your finalization step, not through me."

---

## 10. Versioning

The agent records its own version (schema versions + prompt version) in `agent_version` on every memo draft output. When the schemas change, prior drafts retain their original version stamp. Partners can audit the rules a memo was produced under.

When schemas change mid-flight on an active deal, the default is to finish that deal under the version it started. Partners can opt to re-run with the new schema if they prefer.

body.dealThesis:
Hemrock Ventures invests at Seed and Series A in:

1. **Developer infrastructure and B2B SaaS** with measurable, technical-buyer-validated value. We like products where engineering leadership is the buyer and the cost-of-not-using-the-product is quantifiable in $ saved or $ unlocked.
2. **Vertical SaaS** for underserved buyer types (cooperatives, mid-market trades, regulated niches) where the workflow is sticky and the buyer is consolidated. Bonus for emerging-markets founders with deep domain context.
3. **Instrumentation and analytics** for above categories where the data exhaust becomes the moat.

We avoid:
- Pure B2C / consumer subscription apps without an enterprise wedge
- Hardware, biotech, deep tech with multi-year time-to-revenue
- Crypto, defense, regulated platforms

Check size: $1-3M Seed lead, $1-2M Series A follow-on. We co-invest happily; we don't price-lead Series B and beyond.

Founders we back: technical operators with deep domain context, ideally from a category-defining incumbent (e.g. ex-Vercel for infra, ex-McKinsey-with-domain for vertical SaaS).
